faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Mulund or Bhandup for an evening maths slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is based on the Central Line corridor. We match Mulund, Bhandup and Vikhroli families with tutors from the same stretch or from Ghatkopar and Thane, because the Eastern Express Highway and the Central Line make those hops predictable at 7pm. What rarely holds for a full year is a Western Suburbs tutor crossing to Mulund on a weekday evening; the JVLR and SCLR routes are fine at three in the afternoon and unreliable at seven. For a weekday evening we will offer a local tutor first and reserve the cross-city specialist for a weekend morning or an online slot.

faqs.question: Does our building need to clear the tutor at the gate each week?
faqs.answer: Most Mumbai societies prefer a standing entry for a weekly visitor rather than an approval request every session. Give the gate the tutor's full name as it appears on her identity document, the fixed day and time, and your flat number, and ask the building manager whether a regular visitor pass exists for service providers. It saves the five to ten minutes of gate negotiation that otherwise eats the start of a maths session, which matters more than it sounds when the session is an hour. Tell us if your building bars entries after a set hour, since that rules out some slots entirely.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and we do not know which maths route she is on. How do we find out?
faqs.answer: Open her exercise book and look at the last three weeks. Regression, correlation, modelling tasks and context-heavy word problems indicate Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation. Formal proof, trigonometric identities and heavier algebra indicate Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches. If it is still unclear, email the subject teacher and ask for the full course name and level as entered, not the shorthand. This matters because the two routes examine different skills, and a tutor matched to the wrong one will teach competently and uselessly. We ask for the course name before sending a shortlist for exactly this reason.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the mathematical exploration?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes; with the writing, never. Legitimate help means narrowing an over-ambitious question, building a schedule of dated drafts, teaching the student to read her own draft against the published assessment criteria, explaining what her supervisor's feedback actually asks for, and checking that the mathematics is communicated clearly. Producing text, supplying the mathematics or rewriting sections is academic misconduct and risks the whole Diploma, so refuse any tutor who offers it. Your school's supervisor owns the formal guidance and sets how many check-ins are permitted, so ask the coordinator what support is allowed before the first session.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level maths worth taking if she is borderline?
faqs.answer: Only if two things are true: her target university courses genuinely require it, and she has the weekly hours alongside her other Higher Level subjects. Check the requirement at source, on the universities' own current entry pages and with your school's university counsellor, because requirements vary by country, course and year and nobody should take them from a tutoring page. On the second, a three or four week diagnosis of timed Higher Level questions, marked honestly, tells you more than a term of encouragement. A student who moves to Standard Level and performs is better placed than one who keeps the label and struggles.

faqs.question: What do IB maths tuition fees depend on in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Route and level first, then specialism scarcity, travel distance and session length. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is the narrowest pool in this city, so it sits at the top of any sensible range, while Standard Level and IGCSE tier work sits lower. Travel is the hidden factor: a tutor crossing from Chembur to Borivali twice a week is giving up hours on the road and will price for it. Session shape matters too, since two short online drills plus one home session often costs less than two travelled sessions. We publish the factors rather than a price list; the fees page covers it fully.

faqs.question: She understands in class but freezes in tests. Is that a maths problem?
faqs.answer: Usually it is a timing and method problem rather than a knowledge problem, and it is fixable. The common causes are reading the question too fast, skipping written working so a lost thread cannot be recovered, and spending too long on the first hard question instead of banking the accessible marks. A tutor should diagnose which of the three it is from her actual script rather than guessing. The drill is timed sections with a hard stop, annotating before starting, and reviewing her own paper to classify every lost mark as a gap, a misread or a slip. Classification changes behaviour faster than more teaching does.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough for Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: For a Standard Level student who practises between sessions, often yes. For a Higher Level student with fluency gaps, one session a week usually becomes the tutor re-teaching what was forgotten since the last one. The arrangement that works better is one longer session plus one short midweek slot, because maths fluency responds to frequency rather than duration. The other half of the answer is independent practice: an IB maths home tutor in Mumbai can set and check it, but nobody can do it for your child, and two hours of tutoring a week with no practice between is a predictable disappointment.

faqs.question: Does online maths tuition work for a younger MYP student?
faqs.answer: It can, with one condition: the tutor must be able to see the working as it is written, through a document camera or a phone propped over the page. Without that, online maths for a younger student drifts into watching an explanation, which builds very little. Home classes are the safer default at MYP level because the written method is what the criteria reward and a tutor needs to read it as it forms. We often start younger students at home, establish the habits, and only then add a short online slot for checking work between sessions.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths for two children in different programmes?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single visit covering an IGCSE Extended student and an MYP sibling saves travel and often money. The limit is at Diploma level: a Higher Level specialist is rarely the best person for a much younger child, and dividing a single session between two students usually shortchanges both. The arrangement that works is back-to-back separate sessions in one visit rather than a shared hour. Tell us both children's programmes and levels at the start and we will tell you whether one tutor can honestly carry both.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor turns out to be wrong for her?
faqs.answer: Tell us what specifically is wrong and we change it quickly. A route mismatch, meaning the tutor is teaching the other Diploma course's emphasis, gets a replacement immediately. Pace, rapport or homework structure problems are often fixed by changing the slot or the session length, and we will try that first because continuity matters in a subject that builds on itself. When we do re-match, the new tutor gets the previous notes so your child is not re-diagnosed from zero. Raise it at the four-week review rather than at the end of a term, when a replacement has far less room to work.

sections.heading: How we match a tutor for IB May session exam preparation in Mumbai
paragraphs: Most enquiries about IB May session exam preparation in Mumbai arrive with a subject and a worry attached, and little else. A useful shortlist needs three facts first: which International Baccalaureate (IB) or Cambridge courses your child is entered for and at which level, which examination session the school has entered them for, and how much of each syllabus the class has genuinely finished rather than nominally covered. Families guess at the third. A Diploma Programme (DP) student can be a term behind in Chemistry and ahead in Economics, and one tutor booked for everything fixes neither.

Some enquiries ask for all IB and IGCSE subjects from one tutor in Mumbai, which is rarely the right shape for a final year. Two specialists working two evenings each usually beat one generalist working four, because paper technique is subject-specific and a Physics examiner's habits are not a Business examiner's. Where a child needs broad academic support rather than deep subject work we say so, and we will also tell you when one tutor is genuinely enough and a second would only fill the week.

Geography decides whether a plan survives February. A home tutor who lives across the Western Express Highway from your flat will make the first six weeks and then start arriving late, so we match along a line or a corridor rather than across the city. A tutor in Kandivali East can hold a standing Malad slot through the final term; the same tutor cannot hold a Colaba slot at 6pm, and pretending otherwise wastes the only months that were available.

After that the process is short. You receive two or three profiles carrying the subjects, the series experience and a slot that already accounts for the evening peak. You speak to each tutor before anything is booked. The first session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson: a section of a past paper under time, the last report read properly, a look at the state of the subject file, and a written plan that names what each remaining month before the series covers.

sections.heading: Which courses and levels the May series actually covers
paragraphs: The May series is not one examination. In the same window a DP2 cohort sits Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) papers across six subject groups, the year below may sit Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers, and Middle Years Programme (MYP) students sit whatever their school runs, school-set assessments or on-screen examinations. The preparation these three groups need has very little in common beyond the month on the calendar.

At Diploma level the structural decisions were made a year earlier and they bite now. HL and SL are different courses with different papers, not the same course at two speeds, and a child moved between them in the final year has to unlearn as much as they learn. Cambridge International Education offers Core and Extended tiers in several subjects, and the tier a school has entered a child for sets the range of grades available to them. Your school examinations officer holds the entry record. Ask to see it rather than assuming what it says.

Our coverage line reads all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai, which is awkward English for a plain promise: both boards, every school year, matched by course rather than by subject label. Maths alone is several distinct courses at Diploma level and two tiers at IGCSE. A tutor who knows one of them well is not interchangeable with a tutor who knows another, and the mismatch usually shows up in the third week, when the paper practice starts.

Because paper structures and component names change when a board reissues a subject guide, this page does not list them. Check the current subject guide for your child's course and session, or ask the coordinator which version the class is working from. A tutor who cannot tell you which syllabus version your child sits in May is the wrong tutor, whatever else their profile says.

sections.heading: Where do the internal assessments sit in a May session year?
paragraphs: They sit in the middle of the final year, which is why the autumn term is harder than the spring one. For a May cohort the Internal Assessment (IA) drafts, the Extended Essay (EE) and the Theory of Knowledge (TOK) work cluster in the months when the syllabus is still being taught, not in the revision window where families expect the pressure to arrive.

That overlap is the real pressure point. A DP2 student in Chembur can have a Physics IA draft due the same fortnight as her TOK essay and a Maths test on the Monday after, and the subject she quietly drops is the one with no deadline attached, which is the one she needs in May. A tutor's first job in that fortnight is sequencing rather than teaching: what gets finished, what gets a holding draft, what waits two weeks without damage.

At IGCSE the equivalent pressures are coursework and practical components where a course carries them, plus the oral and speaking components in languages, which schools schedule far earlier than families expect. Subject choice across both boards, HL and SL decisions and Core or Extended tiering all determine which of these your child actually carries, so the honest answer to what is due is specific to one timetable. Ask the coordinator for the internal deadline sheet and build from that, not from a generic calendar.

Where a household needs all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai across two children on two boards, we split the plan by deadline rather than by subject. One child's EE deadline and another's IGCSE coursework submission can land in the same week, and a family that schedules both tutors on the same two evenings loses both. Stagger them, and give the heavier deadline the quieter room.

sections.heading: Mumbai coverage, zone by zone, through the final two terms
paragraphs: Families write to us from across Mumbai, Maharashtra, and IB May session exam preparation in Mumbai is shaped by the zone a child lives in more than by the budget. The phrase parents type is IB tutors near me in Mumbai, and near is the operative word: a tutor who cannot be at your door by a quarter past seven on a Wednesday in February will not be there in March either.

South Mumbai is short on distance and long on time. A tutor crossing from Worli to Cuffe Parade covers very little ground and can still lose most of the evening peak at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals, so island matches stay on the island: Colaba, Fort, Walkeshwar, Tardeo and Breach Candy draw on each other, helped now by the Coastal Road and by Metro Line 3 (Aqua) running from Cuffe Parade to BKC. In the Western Suburbs, matching along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway works and matching across them does not, so Bandra pairs with Khar West and Santacruz West, Malad with Kandivali East and Borivali, with Metro Line 1 between Versova and Ghatkopar via Andheri and Metro Lines 2A and 7 along the Dahisar to Andheri corridor taking some sting out of the north to south run. The Bandra-Worli Sea Link makes a Worli to Bandra match possible, but only for a slot outside the peak.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR and no station of their own, so a Powai tutor is reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar rather than by train. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund West on the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway plus the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) make both the island and the western side reachable from Chembur in a way the map hides. An IB home tutor in Mumbai who commutes on the Harbour Line is worth asking about frequency, because a late train and a 7pm slot do not combine twice in a week.

Navi Mumbai works node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short run from the next on Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, and the Atal Setu has changed what a South Mumbai tutor can reach, though a weekday evening crossing still rarely holds for a full term. Thane spreads from the station east along Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, and Ghodbunder sets the schedule: families in Kasarvadavali and Hiranandani Estate should expect a Thane-based tutor rather than one crossing from Mulund, with the Trans-Harbour Line covering Thane to Vashi for the few who do.

sections.heading: How does the Mumbai school calendar collide with a May series?
paragraphs: It collides twice. The Mumbai academic year opens in June, so a May cohort's final year runs almost end to end against the school calendar, and the two heaviest blocks, the internal assessment season and the school's own mock window, both fall before the spring term where families expect the real work to begin.

In practice the year has a shape worth knowing in advance. The term that opens in June is when a diagnostic is cheap and useful, because nothing is due yet and last year's unfinished topics can still be closed quietly. The months running to the Diwali break carry the IA and essay drafting load. The break itself is the last consolidated run of free days in the year, and families who spend it on one subject's backlog rather than on all four come out ahead. After the break the school's mock window arrives, and from there the calendar belongs to revision.

School expectations differ by campus and they shape the plan. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all work to different internal deadline sheets even when the external series is the same. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page; we build the plan from whatever deadline sheet your school issues.

The dates that matter most are not ours to publish. Examination timetables, entry deadlines, late-entry windows and the school's own study-leave dates come from your school examinations officer, and that is the first person to email once you decide to add a tutor. Ask for the series timetable, the entry confirmation and the internal deadline sheet in one message, then bring all three to the first session so the plan is built against real dates rather than assumptions.
bullets: The June term is the cheapest time to run a diagnostic.
The Diwali break is the last consolidated block of free days.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or both for a May candidate in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the lead service here and for a final-year candidate it is usually right. IB May session exam preparation in Mumbai mostly happens at the table where the child already works, and IB home tuition in Mumbai puts the tutor in front of the folders, the marked scripts and the school's own handouts. In the last two terms that matters far more than it does in Year 9. A tutor who can see the state of a DP2 student's Economics file learns more in ten minutes than a video call tells them in a month.

Online is not the fallback it once was. An IB online tutor in Mumbai solves two problems well: scarce subjects, where the right examiner-experienced teacher for an HL course lives in another zone entirely, and the final weeks, when a forty-minute crossing each way is time your child could have spent on a paper. Screen-shared past papers and annotated scans work properly. What does not travel well is the quiet correction of a working habit, the sideways glance at a page of rough work that shows exactly where a method broke.

Hybrid is what most May candidates end up with, and it is better planned than drifted into. One session a week at home for the teaching and the file discipline, one online for a timed paper and its feedback, is a pattern that survives both traffic and illness. Where a household wants a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai across siblings, hybrid is often the only arrangement in which the week actually fits together.

The honest trade-offs are these. Home classes cost more in travel time and therefore in fee, and they fail first when the tutor's own commute changes mid-term. Online sessions are easier to keep and easier to half-attend, and a child joining from a bedroom with a phone within reach is not studying. One room, one table, the phone outside the door and the same slot every week: both modes need that, and neither mode rescues a plan without it.
bullets: Home sessions let a tutor audit folders, scripts and school handouts.
Online solves scarce subjects and saves crossings in the last weeks.
Hybrid pairs one home session with one timed online paper weekly.
Same room, same slot, phone outside: both modes need this.

sections.heading: How are tutors checked before they reach your building?
paragraphs: Before a tutor is introduced, IB Gram checks identity documents, the degree or teaching qualification claimed, and the teaching history, including a reference call where a school or a previous family can be reached. Board and level experience are checked against the specific course, because IB Diploma teaching and IGCSE teaching are not the same credential and should not be treated as one.

What verification cannot do is predict fit. Parents ask who the best IB tutor in Mumbai is, and the honest answer is that no such person exists in the abstract: there is a right tutor for one child, one course and one series, and the only real test is the first two sessions. So there are checks we run and there are checks you should run yourself, and the second set is the one that protects a final year.

Ask the tutor which syllabus version your child sits and which papers it carries. Ask them to mark one piece of your child's recent work in front of you and explain the marks against the published criteria. Ask how many May candidates they are already carrying this year, because a tutor whose February is full cannot add a sixth evening and will quietly start cancelling. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, or who talks about outcomes before they have read a single script.

Practical checks matter as much as paper ones. A home tutor visiting weekly needs a standing entry in your society's visitor register or a gate pass, and the week before the plan starts is the time to arrange it, not the evening of the first session. Agree in advance who is at home during sessions, where the tutor sits, and what happens to a slot missed on either side, because an unwritten rule about cancellations becomes an argument in March.
bullets: Identity, qualification and teaching history checked before any introduction.
Board and level experience matched to the exact course entered.
Ask for one piece of work marked against the published criteria.
Arrange the society gate pass the week before sessions start.
Agree the missed-session rule in writing before the first week.

sections.heading: The working-backwards plan for a May series, month by month
paragraphs: Build the plan from the series backwards, never from today forwards. IB May session exam preparation in Mumbai works when the shape is written down early: close last year's gaps before the first internal deadline, carry the IA and essay load to the Diwali break, finish syllabus coverage before the school mock window, and spend everything after that on papers. An IB private tutor in Mumbai who starts in June has the whole final year to arrange around that shape; one who starts later is arranging around what is left of it.

From June to the Diwali break the work is coverage and drafting at once. This is also when the northern-hemisphere university cycle starts asking for predicted grades, which come from your child's school and from the work it has actually seen, so a term that feels early is already on the record. A tutor's job in these months is to stop a subject sliding while the essays are being written, not to revise. Revision in September is wasted; the material is not finished and the child has nothing to revise against.

After the break, the hinge is the end of syllabus coverage. Anything still untaught when the spring term opens becomes revision-time debt, and revision time is the one resource a May candidate cannot borrow from anywhere. Mocks sit just before or across that hinge in most schools, and their only job in this plan is to tell you which papers are already safe so attention can go elsewhere. From there the unit of work changes: not the topic any more but the paper, with timed sections, mark schemes read line by line, and the same question type repeated until the method is automatic rather than remembered. The last few weeks are for full papers under conditions and for the mechanics of sitting one.

What a tutor started late can honestly do is narrower, and worth saying plainly. A tutor added in February cannot teach a year of Chemistry in eight weeks and should not claim to try. What they can do is triage: pick the topics that recur in nearly every paper, drill the question types where your child loses marks through habit rather than ignorance, and rehearse the mechanics of a paper, which is worth more in the final month than new content is. A family told that clearly in February is better served than one promised full coverage and handed a timetable nobody can keep.
bullets: Close last year's gaps before the first internal deadline arrives.
Carry essays and IA drafts to the Diwali break, then consolidate.
Syllabus coverage must end before the spring revision term opens.
After mocks the unit of work is the paper, not the topic.
A late start buys triage and exam mechanics, not full coverage.

sections.heading: What a home tutor can realistically change before May
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see mechanics, not marks. An IB tutor in Mumbai working a final-year plan should by then have produced a written diagnosis, a visible change in how your child starts a question, and homework that comes back marked against criteria rather than ticked. If none of that exists after a month, the problem is the match and not the child.

At one term the measure is a timed paper done under conditions and compared with the one from the diagnostic session, section by section rather than as a single total. Expect uneven movement. Paper technique and structured questions improve first; extended writing and multi-step problems improve last. A child who has gone from leaving half a paper blank to attempting every question has made real progress even if the total has barely shifted, because the attempts are where the next gains come from.

Across a full exam cycle the honest statement is simple: we do not guarantee grades, and no tutor can. Results depend on the work your child does between sessions, on the school's teaching, on the level and tier they were entered for, on health in May and on the papers themselves. What a good plan reliably removes is the avoidable loss, the unattempted question, the misread command word, the method that was known but never rehearsed under time pressure.

When it is not working, say so early. If the written plan has not appeared after four weeks, if sessions have drifted into supervised homework, or if your child has stopped speaking during them, ask for a replacement instead of waiting for the term to end. A change made in October costs a fortnight. The same change made in March costs the month you needed for papers, which is exactly why the four-week review exists rather than a term-end one.
bullets: Four weeks: a written diagnosis and marked work, not score jumps.
One term: a timed paper compared with the diagnostic, section by section.
Technique moves first; extended writing and multi-step problems move last.
Ask for a replacement at four weeks, not at the term's end.
Grades are not guaranteed; avoidable losses are what a plan removes.

sections.heading: Starting IB May session exam preparation in Mumbai this month
paragraphs: Starting is a short conversation and a longer first session. Send the subjects and levels, the examination session your child is entered for, your area and the two evening slots that genuinely work, and expect tutor profiles rather than a sales call. The first session with a home tutor is a diagnostic: a section of a past paper under time, the last report read properly, and an honest look at the state of the subject file.

Have four things ready before that session. The school's internal deadline sheet. The entry confirmation from the examinations officer, which settles the course and the level beyond argument. The last two pieces of marked work, including anything returned with criteria attached. And a table that is not the dining table during dinner, with a plug point, a door that closes and a chair nobody else needs.

Expect the plan to be written down and to name months rather than hours. What closes before the Diwali break, what has to finish before the spring term, which papers get rehearsed in the final weeks, and what happens in the gaps between papers once the series has started. A tutor who will not write that down is telling you something useful about how the next eight months would have gone.

If your child's series is not in May, say so at the start. The same method run from a different anchor month produces a completely different plan, and a May timetable is the wrong plan for a child entered elsewhere. Establish which session and which course your child is actually entered for, in writing, before anybody books a term of evenings around it.
bullets: Send subjects, levels, session, area and two workable evening slots.
Have the internal deadline sheet and entry confirmation ready.
Bring two pieces of recently marked work to the first session.
A plan that names months beats a plan that names hours.
Confirm which session your child is entered for before booking.

faqs.question: When should we start preparing for the May session?
faqs.answer: Ideally in the term that opens in June, at the very start of the final year. Nothing is due then, last year's unfinished topics can still be closed cheaply, and a diagnostic costs one session instead of a month. The next best window for IB May session exam preparation in Mumbai is immediately after the Diwali break and before the school's mock period, because the plan can still include teaching. Starting after mocks is common and still useful, but the work changes from coverage to triage. Whenever you begin, ask your school examinations officer for the series timetable and the entry confirmation first, so the plan is built against real dates.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in February for a May series?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change shape and the tutor should say so on the first call. In the last full term nobody can teach a year of content, and a tutor who promises to is telling you they have not looked at the syllabus. What works is triage: the topics that recur in almost every paper, the question types where your child loses marks through habit, and full timed papers with the mark scheme read line by line afterwards. Expect two sessions a week rather than one, and expect to be told which parts of the course you are choosing not to rescue. A February start that is honest beats a June start that drifted.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Peddar Road for an evening slot during exam season?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor already lives on the island. South Mumbai is short on distance and slow in the evening peak, so a Peddar Road slot at 7pm is dependable for a tutor based in Tardeo, Worli or Walkeshwar and unreliable for one coming down from Andheri. The Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 have helped, but a tutor crossing in from the Western Suburbs on a weekday will eventually start arriving late, and in the final term a late arrival costs the timed section. During study leave the better answer is a daytime slot, which removes the traffic problem completely.

faqs.question: What does my society gate need from a home tutor for a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Usually a standing visitor entry rather than a fresh approval every week. Most Mumbai societies accept a resident's written request naming the tutor, the day and the time window, after which the gate logs them against your flat instead of calling up each evening. Arrange it the week before the plan starts: the first session is the worst moment to discover that your tower wants a photo identity upload or a committee approval. Where a society runs an app-based pass or caps visitors during examination months, tell the tutor before the first visit so nobody is left standing at the gate with a folder.

faqs.question: How much does IB tuition cost in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: It depends on five things, and nobody can quote you a real figure without them. IB tuition fees in Mumbai move with the board and level, because Diploma Higher Level work is not priced like IGCSE Core; with subject scarcity, since far fewer people teach HL Physics or a B language than teach middle-school Maths; with travel distance, which is why a tutor crossing from Thane to Bandra costs more than one from Khar West; with session length and frequency; and with how late in the final year you start. Ask for the rate per session and the travel assumption in the same sentence, and get both in writing.

faqs.question: Should we book a home tutor for every subject before the May series?
faqs.answer: No, and four tutors in a final year is usually a sign the diagnosis was skipped. Most May candidates have one or two subjects where the marks are genuinely unsafe and one or two where the child is anxious but competent, and spreading evenings across all of them leaves no time for the independent paper practice that actually moves a score. Start with the two unsafe subjects, give the plan four weeks, and add a third only if a real evening exists for it. A child with no free evening is not preparing for anything, they are commuting between tutors.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a final-year DP student in Thane?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Thane it is often the better choice for a scarce subject. Ghodbunder Road decides the evening, so a Kasarvadavali family looking for an HL Economics specialist may find the right teacher lives in Bandra and will never hold a 7pm weekday slot in person. Online removes that problem entirely. Keep the session at a fixed table with the subject file open and the phone in another room, and ask the tutor to work from scanned past papers rather than slides. Many Thane families run one online session for teaching and one in-person session for the timed paper.

faqs.question: What happens between two papers during the May series itself?
faqs.answer: Very little teaching, and that is correct. Once the series starts, the evening after a paper belongs to the next paper and not to the one just sat, because reading back a finished paper raises anxiety and changes no marks. A tutor's role in that fortnight is narrow: a short session on the next paper's question types, a check that equipment and timetable for the morning are sorted, and a rehearsal of how to open a paper and allocate time across it. Where two papers in one subject sit days apart, that gap belongs to the second paper alone. Your examinations officer confirms the sitting order.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out a month in. What now?
faqs.answer: Tell us at four weeks rather than at the end of term. Say specifically what is missing: no written plan, homework returned unmarked, sessions that have become supervised homework, or a child who has stopped talking during them. That description is what lets us match differently instead of repeating the same mistake with a new face. A replacement starts with the same diagnostic so the new tutor is not working from the old one's notes. In a final year the timing matters more than usual, because a change in October costs a fortnight and the same change in March costs the month you needed for papers.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with the Internal Assessment as well as the written papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the limits your school and the IB set. A tutor can teach the skills an Internal Assessment (IA) is assessing, read a draft the way an examiner reads it, and point at where a criterion is unmet, which is a different act from writing or editing the work. The authorship rules belong to your school's coordinator and the current subject guide, and any tutor working near an IA should know them without being asked. For a May cohort the useful window is the drafting months before the Diwali break, not the week before submission, when all a tutor can do is watch.

faqs.question: What if the results are not what my child hoped for?
faqs.answer: There are two separate routes with different deadlines: a review of results on a specific paper, and re-sitting the subject in a later series. Both run through your school rather than through a tutor, and the windows are short, so the examinations officer is the first call and not the last. A tutor becomes useful afterwards, once you know which components moved and which did not, because a resit plan is built from the component breakdown rather than from the overall score. We do not guarantee grades and will not tell you which route to choose; that decision belongs to the family and the school.

sections.heading: How we match a tutor for IB mock exam preparation in Mumbai
paragraphs: Requests for IB mock exam preparation in Mumbai arrive in two waves, and they need different tutors. The first wave comes six or seven weeks out, when a parent wants the papers prepared for. The second comes in the fortnight after results, when a mock grade has landed badly and the family wants to know what it means. A tutor who is good at the first job is not automatically good at the second, because reading a marked script back is a separate skill from teaching a topic.

So the matching question is which wave you are in. Before mocks, we look for a tutor who will stop teaching new content at the right moment and switch to timed sections. After mocks, we look for someone who will ask for the script rather than the grade, go through it question by question, and come back with a short written list of what actually went wrong. Ask any shortlisted tutor which of those two they think they are being hired for. The answer tells you a great deal.

The practical part follows the usual order. 1. Send the subjects, the levels and the dates of the school mock block if you have them. 2. Tell us whether the scripts have been returned and whether you can get them. 3. Two or three profiles come back with afternoon or weekend slots, because mock fortnight breaks the usual evening pattern. 4. You speak to each tutor before booking. 5. The first session either builds the pre-mock timetable or performs the autopsy on the script, depending on the wave.

Where a household wants a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai because several mocks went badly at once, we will usually push back. Four weak mocks in one block more often reflects a timing or revision-method problem than four separate content problems, and that is one conversation with one tutor rather than four bookings. We would rather fix the method first and see which subjects are still standing afterwards.
bullets: 1. Send subjects, levels and the school mock block dates.
2. Tell us whether the marked scripts can actually be obtained.
3. Profiles come back with afternoon or weekend slots, not only evenings.
4. Speak to each tutor before any booking is made.

sections.heading: Which mocks matter: DP, MYP and IGCSE in Mumbai schools
paragraphs: A mock is set and marked by the school, not by a board, and that single fact explains most of the confusion around them. Two campuses can run a Diploma Programme (DP) mock on the same course with different paper selection, different marking severity and different assumptions about grade boundaries. The International Baccalaureate does not publish your child's mock grade and has no view on it. Only the school does.

The stakes differ by programme. For a DP2 cohort the mock carries real weight because it is a major input into the predicted grades the school sends to universities, which makes it the highest-consequence internal examination of the two years. For Middle Years Programme (MYP) students a mock is mostly diagnostic and worth treating calmly. At Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE a mock can carry a decision attached to it, because some schools use mock performance as evidence when confirming whether a child is entered at Core or Extended tier, and that entry decision shapes the range of grades available. Ask your school whether the mock plays that role before treating it as a dry run.

Level discipline matters in the preparation. A Higher Level (HL) mock and a Standard Level (SL) mock in the same subject are not the same paper, and a tutor preparing a child for the wrong one wastes the weeks that mattered. Our coverage line reads all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai, and the operative words there are course and level rather than subject. Confirm which paper your child is actually sitting in the mock block, because schools occasionally run a shortened or combined version.

One thing a mock does not test is coursework, and that catches families out every year. Internal Assessment (IA) work, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) components sit outside the mock entirely, so a child can sit a strong mock block while an IA draft is three weeks late. If you are using the mock as a progress check, check the coursework position separately with the coordinator in the same week.
bullets: A mock is set and marked by the school, not by a board.
DP mocks feed predicted grades; MYP mocks are mostly diagnostic.
Ask whether an IGCSE mock informs the Core or Extended entry.

sections.heading: What does a mock paper test that a class test does not?
paragraphs: Four things, and none of them is content knowledge. A mock tests breadth across a whole course rather than a recent unit, the decisions involved in choosing questions, the pacing of a full paper from first question to last, and the reading of command words under pressure. A child who scores well on unit tests and badly in a mock usually has a complete content base and no examination technique.

Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai sees the same pattern repeating. In the sciences, marks go on data handling and on explanations that state what happened without saying why. In Mathematics, method marks are lost because working is not written down, so a right answer reached badly scores less than a wrong answer reasoned well. In the essay subjects, the loss is almost always structure and the command word: a question that says evaluate answered as though it said describe will score in the lower band however much the student knows. In languages, timing on the longer writing task is the usual culprit.

Question choice deserves its own attention because it is pure technique and completely teachable. Where a paper offers options, students pick the question with the familiar topic rather than the one with the answerable question, and then write everything they know instead of what was asked. A tutor can rehearse this in twenty minutes a week: read all the options, mark the command word, sketch the answer in three lines, then choose. Children who do that in a mock stop losing whole bands in the real series.

Breadth is the other mock-specific problem. A class test covers what was taught in the last month, so a child can carry a forgotten first-year topic for a long time without consequence. A mock paper will find it. That is the single most useful thing a mock does, and it is why the weeks after one are worth more than the weeks before.
bullets: Mocks test breadth, pacing, question choice and command words.
Unwritten working in Mathematics loses method marks silently.
Evaluate answered as describe scores in a lower band regardless.

sections.heading: Mock weeks across Mumbai: school clusters and afternoon slots
paragraphs: Mock season changes the shape of the week, and that is the local story here. During the block, school days end early or stop entirely, so the useful slot moves from 7pm to the afternoon, and at 3pm this city is a different place. A tutor who could never hold an evening slot across the Western Express Highway can hold a four o'clock one comfortably. So mock fortnight is the one period when parents searching IB tutors near me in Mumbai should widen the radius rather than narrow it.

School clusters matter more than residential zones for this. In South Mumbai, families around Fort, Napean Sea Road, Breach Candy, Worli and Mahalaxmi are mostly at island campuses, and an afternoon session there avoids the Peddar Road and Haji Ali crawl entirely, with the Coastal Road and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link useful for the rarer cross-city match and Metro Line 3 running underneath. In the Western Suburbs the heavy cluster runs from Bandra West and Santacruz West through Juhu to Goregaon East, with Kandivali East and Borivali further up; Metro Line 1 between Versova and Ghatkopar and Metro Lines 2A and 7 along the Dahisar to Andheri corridor make an afternoon crossing straightforward where the Western Line is crowded.

In the Central Suburbs the clusters sit around Powai, Ghatkopar, Bhandup and Mulund West, reached by road through JVLR and the Eastern Express Highway or on the Central Line. The Eastern Suburbs, from Wadala and Chembur out to Govandi and Vikhroli, have the Harbour Line, the Eastern Freeway and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR), and a Chembur family can reasonably look at a tutor on the island for an afternoon slot in mock week even though an evening one would never hold.

Navi Mumbai and Thane work on their own clocks. In Navi Mumbai, Nerul, Seawoods, Belapur and Kharghar are a few minutes apart on Palm Beach Road, so a node-to-node afternoon match is easy and the Atal Setu widens the weekend options for a paper review. In Thane, families in Thane West, Hiranandani Estate, Pokhran Road and Kasarvadavali should still favour a tutor on their side of Ghodbunder Road, though the afternoon version of that road is a different animal from the seven o'clock one. Families write to us from right across Mumbai, Maharashtra, and in this fortnight the right answer is usually the tutor who can be free at 4pm.
bullets: Mock fortnight moves the useful slot from 7pm to mid-afternoon.
Widen the search radius during mocks; afternoon traffic allows it.

sections.heading: When do Mumbai schools run mock exams?
paragraphs: Each school sets its own mock window, so there is no city-wide answer and nobody should give you one. For a cohort sitting the May series, the mock block usually falls in the winter term, after the long Diwali break and before the spring revision term. For a cohort sitting the November series the school's window was built for May candidates, so an out-of-cycle student often needs a mock arranged specially. Your school examinations officer holds the actual dates, and they are the person to ask.

What families should ask for alongside the dates is the shape of the block. How many papers in how many days, whether they are sat in examination conditions or in classrooms, whether the full paper is used or a shortened version, how long until scripts come back, and whether scripts come back at all. Those answers change the preparation more than the dates do. A block of eight papers in five days needs stamina work in the fortnight before; the same eight spread over three weeks does not.

Standards vary between campuses, which is why mock grades travel badly between families. Parents at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Gopi Birla Memorial School in Walkeshwar, Activity High School on Peddar Road, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, JBCN International School in Borivali and in Oshiwara, Witty International School in Malad, Billabong High International School in Santacruz, Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul are all comparing numbers produced under different conditions. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here; we work from your child's script and your school's own marking, not from a comparison.

The other school conversation worth having early is about predicted grades. They are issued by the school, informed by the mock and by everything else the teachers have seen, and a tutor has no part in setting them. If a mock grade is going to affect a university application, the discussion belongs with the subject teacher and the counsellor in the fortnight after results, while the script and the reasoning are still fresh. Going in with a marked paper and three specific questions works far better than going in with a complaint.
bullets: Each campus sets its own mock window; ask for your dates.
Ask how many papers in how many days, and in what conditions.
Find out whether marked scripts are returned, and how quickly.
Mock grades from different schools are not comparable numbers.
Predicted grades are the school's; raise them with the subject teacher.

sections.heading: Home tuition or online classes for the weeks around mocks
paragraphs: Home tutoring leads for the paper work, and most IB mock exam preparation in Mumbai happens at a dining table for a physical reason. A marked script is a paper object covered in a teacher's handwriting, and IB home tuition in Mumbai means a tutor sitting next to your child with that script flat on the table, a pen in hand and the mark scheme beside it. Scanning eight papers to send ahead of a video call is possible and almost nobody does it. The same session at home needs no preparation beyond finding the folder.

Online earns its place in the timed-paper half of the work. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can set a paper, start a shared timer, stay silent for the duration and then mark it live on screen, which is a well-suited use of the format and saves two crossings in a week when every afternoon counts. It also makes a short session practical: fifteen minutes on tomorrow's paper structure during the mock block itself is worth having and is not worth a commute in either direction.

The hybrid that works around mocks is specific enough to name. In the weeks before, run the teaching and the timed papers wherever is convenient. During the block, go online for short daily contact and nothing more. In the fortnight after, go back home for the script autopsy, because that session needs the paper, the mark scheme and two people looking at the same page. Agree that pattern when you book rather than renegotiating it mid-block.

Honest trade-offs, as always. Home classes cost travel time and therefore fee, and during mock fortnight they also cost flexibility, since a session fixed for Tuesday afternoon cannot move when the school changes a paper date. Online is flexible and loses the shared page. Neither mode helps if the household treats mock week as normal: the child needs the quiet room, an early night and somebody else answering the door.
bullets: Script review needs the paper on a table, so do it at home.
Online suits timed papers: shared timer, silence, live marking after.
Short daily online contact during the block beats a long session.
Return home for the autopsy fortnight, with mark scheme in hand.
A fixed afternoon slot cannot move when the school shifts a paper.

sections.heading: Who marks your child's mock, and how is a tutor checked?
paragraphs: Your child's mock is marked by their own subject teacher in most schools, which is worth knowing before anybody argues with a grade. That teacher has the class standard, the paper and the context; what they do not always have is time to annotate every lost mark. IB Gram checks a tutor's identity, qualifications and teaching history with a reference call before any introduction, and for this work we also check whether they have marked to published criteria themselves.

That last check is the one that matters for mock work. A tutor who has examined or who has taught the course long enough to mark a paper against the scheme will tell you why a four-mark answer scored two. A tutor who has not will tell you the answer was incomplete, which you already knew. Ask directly: have you marked this paper type against the published scheme, and will you show me how the marks fall on one of my child's answers?

Run your own checks beyond that. Ask an IB private tutor in Mumbai how they would spend the first session if the script has not come back yet, because there is a real answer involving the question paper alone and a vague one. Ask what they will not do, which should include writing your child's coursework and predicting a grade. No honest tutor offers a guaranteed grade off the back of a mock, and anybody who talks about outcomes before reading a script is guessing in front of you.

Then the practical household checks, which do not change for mock season except in timing. A home tutor arriving at 4pm on a weekday needs the same standing gate pass or visitor entry as one arriving at 7pm, and daytime entry sometimes needs a different approval in a society that logs school-hours visitors separately. Sort it before the block starts, agree who is at home in the afternoon, and agree what happens to a slot when the school moves a paper.
bullets: Most mocks are marked by your child's own subject teacher.
Ask whether the tutor has marked this paper type to the scheme.
Ask them to show the marks falling on one real answer.
Daytime society entry can need a separate approval from evening entry.
Agree now what happens when the school moves a paper date.

sections.heading: How to read a mock paper back, and what a mock score does not tell you
paragraphs: The grade on the front is the least useful number on the paper. Real IB mock exam preparation in Mumbai starts after the mock, with the script open and every lost mark sorted into one of four causes: content never taught, content taught and forgotten, method understood but misapplied, and marks lost to timing or to a misread command word. Those four demand completely different responses, and a plan that treats them as one thing fails.

Work through it in order. Content never taught is not your child's problem and not the tutor's first priority either; note it, tell the school, and check whether the mock covered material the class had not reached, which happens more often than families assume. Content taught and forgotten is the cheapest fix available and belongs in short weekly retrieval work rather than in re-teaching. Method misapplied is the expensive one, because the child believes they know it, and it needs supervised practice on the same question type until the method is automatic. Timing and command-word losses are technique, and they move fastest of all: usually within three or four sessions, which is why a page of them in a mock is good news.

Now what a mock score cannot tell you. It cannot tell you a grade, because the school chose the papers and set the marking severity and may have used its own boundaries. It cannot tell you about a topic the paper never asked about. It cannot tell you whether your child was unwell that week. And a single harsh mock cannot tell you more than a term of marked class work, so when the two disagree, treat the disagreement itself as the finding and go and ask the teacher which one surprised them. The honest output of a mock is the distribution of lost marks, not the total.

The fortnight after the block is the whole opportunity, and it is short. The script is fresh in your child's memory for about ten days, after which they genuinely cannot remember what they were thinking in question seven, and the autopsy degrades into guesswork. So ask for the scripts early, sit down with an IB home tutor in Mumbai while the memory holds, produce one page of written actions per subject, and then re-sit one full paper under time three or four weeks later to see which of the four causes actually moved. That one page per subject is the most valuable document a mock produces.
bullets: Sort every lost mark into one of four distinct causes.
Forgotten content is cheap to fix; misapplied method is not.
Timing and command-word losses move within three or four sessions.
A mock score reflects the school's paper choice and marking severity.
The script is reliable in memory for about ten days, so hurry.

sections.heading: What home classes can change between mocks and the real series
paragraphs: In the first fortnight, expect a document rather than a difference. An IB tutor in Mumbai doing this work properly should hand you one page per subject: the four causes with your child's actual lost marks under each, what will be done about each, and in what order. If the first two sessions produce encouragement and no page, the work has not happened.

By four to six weeks the test is a re-sat paper, the same paper type under the same time limit, compared with the mock section by section. Technique losses should be visibly down, because they are the fastest to move. Forgotten content should be down if retrieval practice happened. Misapplied method may barely have shifted, and that is normal rather than a failure; it is the slowest of the four and the one that needs the most supervised repetition. Parents who look only at the total will miss all of that.

Across the stretch between mocks and the real series, the honest limits. We do not guarantee grades and nobody can predict one from a mock. The variables that remain are the work done between sessions, the school's own teaching, the papers that turn up on the day and your child's health in the exam fortnight. Parents often ask us to find the best IB tutor in Mumbai after a bad mock, and the more useful request is a tutor who can read a script, because that skill is specific and checkable while the superlative is not.

If nothing has changed six weeks after the mock, the match is wrong and the clock is now expensive. Say what is missing: no written page, no re-sat paper, sessions that have become homework supervision. A replacement after mocks still has the remaining term to work with, and the new tutor should start from the same script rather than from the previous tutor's notes. Leaving it until the next set of internal exams wastes the one diagnostic your child already paid for in a week of papers.
bullets: First fortnight: one written page per subject, not encouragement.
Four to six weeks: the same paper type re-sat under time.
Technique improves first; misapplied method is the slowest to move.
Grades are not guaranteed, and no mock predicts one.
Replace a wrong match at six weeks, not at the next exams.

sections.heading: Starting mock preparation in Mumbai this fortnight
paragraphs: Send three things and the match is usually quick: the subjects and levels, the mock block dates if the school has issued them, and whether the marked scripts are in your hands yet. The third one decides what the first session is for. With scripts, it is an autopsy. Without them, it is a timetable built from the question papers and the last set of class marks.

Prepare the table before the session rather than during it. The question papers, the marked scripts, the subject file, a highlighter and a blank sheet per subject. Where a school returns scripts only on request, ask for them in writing early, and where it does not return them at all, ask whether your child may read their paper in school and note the question numbers where marks went. Even a list of question numbers is enough to start.

Expect the tutor to spend the first session mostly reading and asking your child what they were thinking, which can look like very little teaching for the money. It is the part that makes the next six weeks efficient. Where several subjects went wrong at once, all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai are not the answer; one tutor diagnosing the method is, and the subject bookings follow from what they find.

One last thing to settle before anybody books. Confirm with the school which examination session your child is entered for and which paper the mock used, because mock preparation for a cohort sitting in a few months looks nothing like mock preparation for a cohort a year out. Establish the real entry first, in writing, and the plan after that is straightforward.
bullets: Send subjects, levels, mock block dates and script availability.
Lay out papers, scripts, file, highlighter and a blank sheet.
Ask in writing for scripts early; a question-number list will do.
One diagnostic tutor first, subject bookings after the findings.
Confirm the entered session and the mock paper before booking.

faqs.question: How long before mocks should a tutor start?
faqs.answer: Six to seven weeks is the useful window for IB mock exam preparation in Mumbai, and the shape of it matters more than the length. The first few weeks close the content gaps the class has already covered but your child has not consolidated, the middle weeks move to timed sections, and the last two weeks are full papers with no new material at all. Starting two weeks out is still worth doing, but it becomes technique work only: question choice, pacing, command words and the mechanics of sitting a paper. Ask the school for the mock block dates first so the countdown is built on the real timetable rather than on a guess.

faqs.question: My child's mock grade is far below their class marks. Which one is right?
faqs.answer: Probably neither on its own, and the gap between them is the actual finding. Class marks measure recent material in short tests; a mock measures the whole course under time, so a wide gap usually points at breadth and pacing rather than at understanding. Get the script and sort the lost marks by cause before drawing any conclusion. Then take the paper to the subject teacher and ask one question: was this result a surprise? If it was, something specific happened in that room on that day. If it was not, the teacher has been seeing something the class tests did not show you.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come home for an afternoon slot during mock week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and mock week is the easiest fortnight of the year to arrange it. School days finish early or stop during the block, so a 3pm or 4pm session is possible for the first time, and afternoon traffic across this city is nothing like the evening peak. That widens your choice of tutor considerably. Two conditions: tell the tutor the block dates as soon as the school issues them, because every family in the cluster wants the same afternoons, and check that whoever is at home can let the tutor in during school hours. A slot nobody can open the door for is not a slot.

faqs.question: Will my building let a tutor in for a daytime slot during mocks?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, but it can need a separate approval from an evening visit. Several societies log school-hours visitors differently, some require a resident present rather than domestic staff, and a few run an app-based pass that has to be issued each time. Sort this in the week before the mock block, not on the first afternoon. Ask your society office for a standing entry naming the tutor, the days and the time window, and send the tutor whatever the gate will want to see. During mock fortnight a tutor stuck at the gate for twenty minutes costs you a paper review you cannot reschedule.

faqs.question: Do mock results decide predicted grades?
faqs.answer: They inform them heavily but they do not decide them, and the decision is the school's alone. Predicted grades are issued by your child's teachers using the mock, class work, coursework progress and their own judgement of trajectory, which is why a single weak paper in one subject rarely moves a prediction by itself and a consistent pattern does. No tutor has any role in setting a prediction, and you should be sceptical of one who implies otherwise. If a prediction matters for an application, book time with the subject teacher and the school counsellor in the fortnight after results, with the marked script in hand.

faqs.question: What do we do with the marked mock script?
faqs.answer: Take it apart within ten days, while your child can still remember what they were thinking. Go question by question and put every lost mark into one of four buckets: never taught, taught and forgotten, method misapplied, or lost to timing and command words. Write one page per subject listing what falls where and what will be done about each. Then put the script in the subject file rather than the bin, because it is the comparison point when the same paper type is re-sat in a month. Families who file the grade and lose the paper have thrown away the only diagnostic the week produced.

faqs.question: Should we book extra sessions during the mock fortnight itself?
faqs.answer: Shorter ones, not extra ones. During the block the only useful work is on tomorrow's paper: fifteen or twenty minutes on its structure, the question types and the timing plan, plus a check that equipment and the timetable are sorted. Long teaching sessions in the middle of a mock block cost sleep and return very little, and reading back a paper already sat raises anxiety without changing a mark. Keep the heavy work for the fortnight after results. Where a tutor wants to add two-hour sessions during the block itself, ask them what the student is meant to do with the material that night.

faqs.question: How much does mock preparation cost in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: It depends on the same factors as any other engagement, plus one specific to this work. IB tuition fees in Mumbai move with board and level, with subject scarcity, with travel distance, and with session length and frequency. The mock-specific factor is marking time: a tutor who reads and annotates a full script between sessions is doing unpaid work unless it is priced in, so ask whether script review is included in the session rate or charged separately. Get the per-session rate, the travel assumption and the marking arrangement in one written message before the first session, and ask what a short mock-week session costs.

faqs.question: Does a weak mock at a Powai school mean a tier change at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Not by itself, and the decision sits with the school rather than with you or a tutor. Some schools do use mock performance as part of the evidence when confirming whether a child is entered at Core or Extended tier, so a weak mock can start that conversation. Ask the examinations officer directly what the entry currently says and what would change it, and ask the subject teacher what they would need to see to keep an Extended entry. Then build the next six weeks around that answer. A tier decision taken on one paper, without asking what caused the lost marks, is a decision taken too early.

faqs.question: The tutor wants to stop teaching new content before mocks. Is that right?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a good sign rather than a worrying one. In the last two weeks before a paper, new content displaces the rehearsal that actually converts knowledge into marks, and a topic learned three days before a mock is rarely available under time pressure. The right use of those weeks is full papers, mark schemes read properly and the question types your child loses marks on. Any genuinely missing topic should be noted for the weeks after mocks instead. A tutor still introducing new material the week before the block has not planned the six weeks that preceded it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Kharghar for a weekend paper review session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the weekend is the right time to ask for it. Navi Mumbai matches well node to node, so a tutor from Nerul, Belapur or Panvel reaches Kharghar easily on Palm Beach Road or the Sion-Panvel Highway, and a weekend crossing from the island city over the Atal Setu is realistic in a way the same trip at 7pm on a Wednesday is not. A script review is the ideal session to put on a Saturday morning: it needs ninety unhurried minutes, the papers spread out on a table and nobody watching the clock for a school bus.

ib-mock-exam-preparation.closingCta: Send the subjects and levels, the mock block dates if the school has published them, and whether the marked scripts are in your hands. Two or three tutor profiles come back with afternoon and weekend slots, because mock fortnight does not run on evenings. You speak to each one before booking, and the first home tutor session produces one written page per subject: every lost mark sorted by cause, with what happens next.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram match an IB MYP arts home tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: IB Gram matches on three things: the art form your child is actually doing, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) year they are in, and how far a tutor can realistically travel on a weekday evening. You send the school, the year, the art form and your locality. We come back with two or three verified tutors and you speak to each one before anything is booked. An IB MYP arts home tutor in Mumbai is matched to the art form first, because visual arts, music, drama and dance are not interchangeable and a painter is no help to a child building a dance composition.

The art form question matters more here than in almost any other MYP subject group. A tutor who studied fine art can read a sketchbook and talk about mark-making, but will not hear why a student's recorder piece sits awkwardly in its register. Within visual arts there is a further split: a printmaker, an illustrator and a sculptor teach different things and notice different problems. We ask which medium the current unit uses before we shortlist, and if the school has set a unit no available tutor has worked in, we say so rather than sending someone to improvise in front of a thirteen-year-old.

The second filter is distance, and in Mumbai that is a question about roads rather than kilometres. A tutor living in Chembur can take a standing Tuesday slot in Govandi and hold it for a whole term. The same tutor offered Bandra at 6pm will cancel by week four. We match within a corridor wherever the art form allows it, and when a specialism is scarce enough that nobody nearby covers it, we say that plainly and offer online sessions or a weekend home slot instead of pretending the weekday run across the city will hold.

sections.heading: The MYP years, the eight subject groups, and where arts sits
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, usually Years 6 to 10 in a Mumbai school's own numbering, and it covers eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, design, and physical and health education. Arts is one group holding two broad families, visual arts and performing arts, and performing arts in most Mumbai schools means music, drama or dance. A student may stay with one art form for the whole programme or rotate through two or three in the early years before settling.

What changes across the five years is not the criteria but the expectation sitting behind them. In MYP Year 1 a student may be asked to look at one artist and try something similar. By Year 4 the same student is expected to run an enquiry: find practitioners doing something relevant to their own question, test techniques, keep a record, and explain what the testing changed. By Year 5 the written reflection is read as seriously as the finished piece, and students who have only ever been praised for neat work find that shift uncomfortable. It is a change of job, not a change of difficulty.

Two things sit outside this page. The Year 5 personal project is its own piece of work with a school-appointed supervisor, and we cover it separately. MYP eAssessment is a school decision: some Mumbai schools enter Year 5 students for external assessment and others report on internally moderated work, and only your school's MYP coordinator can confirm which route applies. Requests reach us in many shapes, from a MYP subject groups tutor in Mumbai to MYP subject groups home classes Mumbai parents describe in one line, and the internal label we file them under is MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai, which is unwieldy but accurate. What we need from you is narrower: art form, year, locality.

Visual arts, music, drama and dance need different specialists, not one generalist

sections.heading: Criteria A to D in MYP arts, and what each one is really asking
paragraphs: MYP arts is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, and they run in the order a real project runs: investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. Your school publishes the current wording and the band descriptors on the task sheet it hands out, and the IB revises subject guides on its own cycle, so take the bands from the sheet in your child's folder rather than from any summary, including this one. What does not change is the shape. Two of the four criteria are about thinking, one is about making, and one is about looking back honestly.

Here is the gap in practice. A Year 4 student in Khar West is cutting a series of lino prints about the Mithi River. For the investigating criterion she has to show she looked at practitioners doing something related, named them properly, and said what she took from them and what she rejected. For the evaluating criterion she has to say what the finished prints did not manage to do. Most students write the first reasonably and the second as an apology. A tutor's job is to make her say, in one plain sentence, what the third pull taught her that the first two did not.

The commonest pattern that IB MYP arts home tuition in Mumbai has to fix is a folder of competent work with almost nothing written around it. The making is fine. The student can talk about it fluently when asked a direct question. None of it is on the page, and a moderator reads pages. A tutor who knows the criteria will spend the first few weeks mostly on writing and talking, which can feel to a parent like the art has stopped happening. It has not. The art was never the missing part, and saying so early saves an argument in February.
bullets: Criterion A: investigating practitioners, naming what was taken and rejected
Criterion B: developing skills through recorded, dated experiments
Criterion C: the making or the performance itself
Criterion D: evaluating honestly, including what the work failed to do
Take band wording from the school task sheet, not from online summaries

sections.heading: Where across Mumbai an MYP arts home tutor can reach you
paragraphs: IB Gram places tutors across Mumbai, Maharashtra, and in arts the geography decides more than families expect, because a late tutor eats the only hour the paints are out. South Mumbai is short on distance and long on time: a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers a few kilometres and can lose forty minutes at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals. So an IB MYP arts home tutor in Mumbai working with Cuffe Parade, Colaba, Fort, Walkeshwar or Worli families is matched inside the island, reachable on the Western Line out of Churchgate, the Harbour Line from CSMT, Metro Line 3 or the Coastal Road.

The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, and matching along that line works far better than matching across it. Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri West, Goregaon East, Malad, Kandivali and Borivali are all covered, with Metro Line 1 linking Versova, Andheri and Ghatkopar, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 running Dahisar to Gundavali. The Bandra-Worli Sea Link makes a Worli to Bandra run workable on a Saturday morning and useless at half past six on a Tuesday. A music tutor living in Malad will take Kandivali and Borivali happily and quietly resent Bandra, so we do not ask.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off the JVLR between them. Powai has no station of its own, so tutors reach it by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) decides whether a Kurla slot holds through monsoon. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway puts Wadala and Chembur closer to South Mumbai than the map suggests, which is why a few SoBo-based arts tutors will take an Eastern Suburbs evening.

Navi Mumbai is built in nodes and we match node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Harbour Line and the Navi Mumbai Metro between them. The Atal Setu has made the island city reachable, but a tutor crossing it twice a week for a weekday lesson rarely lasts a full term. Thane spreads from the station out along Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, and Ghodbunder sets the clock: Kasarvadavali is twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour at seven in the evening, which is why Thane students are matched to Thane tutors.

sections.heading: Which Mumbai school calendars set the MYP arts deadlines?
paragraphs: The Mumbai IB school year runs roughly June to April, and MYP arts deadlines cluster in three places: a first summative task in August or September, an exhibition or performance window somewhere across October to December, and a final submission with written reflection in February or March. Your school's own assessment calendar is the only authority on the actual dates. Ask the arts teacher for it in June, and put the three clusters in a shared family calendar before anything else gets booked into those weeks.

Families using IB Gram have children at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Oberoi International School in Goregaon East (JVLR), Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, JBCN International School, Parel, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, NES International School in Mulund West and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Navi Mumbai. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools, or with the International Baccalaureate organisation. We name them because their calendars and their art rooms are what a tutor has to plan around, nothing more.

The pressure point most families miss is the October to November stretch, when a school arts exhibition, the Diwali break and the mid-year reporting cycle land on top of each other. A Year 5 student with a performance in the first week of November stops making new work for three weeks beforehand, and the journal entries stop with it. A tutor who has worked a Mumbai school year before will pull the written reflection forward into September so that November is only about the performance. IB home tuition in Mumbai is at its most useful in September, not in March, and that sequencing is worth more than extra hours in January.
