sections.heading: When do Mumbai schools set the investigation tasks that matter?
paragraphs: Most Mumbai international schools set their first substantial assessed investigation somewhere between late September and November, and a second heavier run from February to the close of the year in March or April. Schools here open in June and work in two semesters, so the opening weeks are settling and revision, and the first task that genuinely tests Criterion B thinking usually arrives once the monsoon has eased. That is the task that tells you whether your child has ever been taught to justify anything.

Families using IB Gram come from across the city's IB and IGCSE schools: Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Dhirubhai Ambani International School and Ascend International School in BKC, Oberoi International School on JVLR at Goregaon East, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Podar International School in Santacruz and Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, JBCN International School at Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. They are named here as local context. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any of these schools or with the International Baccalaureate organisation, and nothing on this page should be read as a school endorsement.

The calendar matters for stretch work in a way it does not for repair work. Depth takes months and shows up in a single assessed task, so a tutor who starts in July has two clear runs at the student before the heavy February stretch. A tutor who starts in late January is working inside someone else's deadline and will end up supporting rather than stretching, which is a waste of a strong student's evenings. Mumbai families also lose two predictable windows every year: the Diwali break, when standing slots lapse and are hard to restart, and the fortnight around the winter holidays.

One more scheduling point that catches families out. Year 5 students carry the personal project alongside mathematics, and schools time it differently; at some it overlaps precisely with the February assessment run. If your child is in Year 5, ask the MYP coordinator for the project timeline in writing at the start of the year and plan the mathematics slot around it rather than discovering the clash in week three of a crisis.

sections.heading: Why home classes suit a capable MYP mathematician in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tutoring leads for this intent because stretch work is physical in a way that repair work is not. The tutor needs to see the page while it is being written, not after. When a student who finds mathematics easy is given a question with no obvious method, what matters is the first ninety seconds: do they pick up the pen, do they draw something, do they try a small case, or do they look up. None of that survives a video call cleanly, and a strong student knows exactly how to look busy on a screen. An IB MYP extended mathematics home tutor in Mumbai sitting across the table can read the difference between thinking and stalling, and can leave a silence long enough to matter.

Online is genuinely better in three situations and we say so. When the depth you need does not exist in your corridor, an IB online tutor in Mumbai is better than the nearest available compromise, and for a student who is already strong the quality of the tutor outweighs the format. When the family travels, which Mumbai families do over Diwali and through May, online keeps the rhythm rather than breaking it for six weeks. And a short mid-week review of marked work does not justify a forty minute drive in either direction. The trade-off is real: written working is harder to supervise, and younger MYP students generally do better with a parent within earshot rather than behind a closed door.

Hybrid is where a lot of Mumbai families land and it is worth choosing deliberately. A ninety minute session at home on a weekend morning for new depth work and investigation practice, plus a thirty to forty minute online session mid-week to look at what the student produced on their own. The weekend session is where the hard question is set and the silence is held. The midweek session is where the writing gets picked apart. For families in Kharghar, Panvel or along Ghodbunder Road, where a weekday evening journey is the weakest link in any plan, hybrid is often the only version that survives a full year.

Frequency is the question families get wrong most often. Twice a week is usually wrong for stretch work and right for repair. A capable student needs time between sessions to sit with a hard problem, get nowhere for two days and come back to it, which is the exact experience the Extended route is trying to build. One substantial session a week with real work in between beats two short ones that leave no gap for anything to happen in. IB home tuition in Mumbai is often sold by the hour, and more hours is not the upgrade it appears to be here.

sections.heading: Checking a home tutor who will teach above their comfort zone
paragraphs: Every tutor is checked on identity with a government photo document, on qualification with the actual subject degree certificate, and on teaching history with named schools or institutions and contactable references. For an IB MYP extended mathematics home tutor in Mumbai we add one more filter, because the usual checks do not catch the failure mode here. A tutor can be fully qualified, thoroughly verified, highly experienced with students who need help, and still have nothing to offer a student who does not. The check for this intent is a working one: we ask the tutor to produce a hard question in a topic a strong Year 9 student has already finished, and we look at what they produce.

There are things you should check yourself in the first two sessions, and they are easy to observe from the next room. Does the tutor set a question and then stop talking. Does the student spend more of the hour writing than listening. Does the tutor ever say they are not sure and work it out alongside the student, which is a good sign rather than a worrying one. Does the work coming out of the session look different from the school's homework, or has the hour become a supervised version of it. Parents looking at results from searches for IB tutors near me Mumbai will get a list of credentials; none of those four things appear on a profile.

Ask direct questions at the introduction call. Which MYP years and which route have you taught? What would you do if my child finishes your hard question in four minutes? How do you teach a student to write up a justification? What does your session look like when the student gets nowhere for the whole hour, and is that a failure? An IB private tutor Mumbai families find through a building group can be excellent and should face the same four questions. Be wary of anyone who promises a specific grade or a fixed improvement, because that is not a claim an honest teacher can make about a student they have not met.

One boundary never moves. A tutor may teach, set practice, discuss an approach in general terms, and mark work the student has already written. A tutor may never write, draft, part-draft or supply any portion of work that will be submitted for assessment, including an investigation task and any section of the Year 5 personal project. This is the point at which stretch work carries a particular risk, because a capable student under deadline pressure is exactly who gets offered that kind of help. If it is offered, end the arrangement and tell us. The consequences land on your child and not on the adult who suggested it.

sections.heading: Is my child bored or struggling with Extended mathematics?
paragraphs: Boredom and difficulty produce almost identical behaviour at home, which is why so many families get this wrong in both directions. Homework is not done, or is done carelessly. Marks slip a little. The student says the subject is boring, or says nothing at all. They avoid starting. They make errors a parent knows they are well past making. A parent seeing that list usually reaches for one of two explanations, depending on what they already believe about their child, and then buys the wrong kind of help for a year.

The test that separates them is a single hard question, set without warning and without a method. Give a student who is bored a problem that genuinely resists them and watch what happens: they lean in, they argue, they want to know if they got it, and they are often a little annoyed that it took so long. Give the same problem to a student who is struggling and the response is different in kind, not degree: they wait, or they ask what topic it is from, or they produce a method that belongs to a different question because they are searching for a procedure rather than thinking about the situation. The first student is under-fed. The second is being asked for something nobody has taught them yet, which is a teaching gap and not a failing of theirs.

Both are fixable and neither says anything permanent about a child. The bored student needs depth and the freedom to work on something for a week without being rescued. The student who is finding Extended heavy needs the missing skill named precisely and taught directly: how to start an unfamiliar problem, how to try a small case, how to write a justification. The mistake is treating the second as a motivation problem or the first as a capability one. Both responses make the behaviour worse, because both tell the student that the adults around them have misread the situation, which thirteen-year-olds notice quickly and resent.

A tutor can usually tell you which you have after two or three sessions, and should put it in writing with the evidence. If the conclusion is that the Extended route is not a good fit for how this student wants to use their time, that is information for a conversation with the MYP coordinator, who decides route questions with you. It is not a verdict and a tutor cannot make the call. Our own listing line, MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai, is a mouthful, and this diagnosis is the part of the service that actually earns its place.

sections.heading: What a stretched student looks like after a term in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks, look for appetite rather than marks. The student complains that a problem is hard and then keeps going. They bring a question to the tutor instead of waiting to be given one. They start writing within the first minute of an unfamiliar question rather than reading it four times. Nothing may have been assessed in that window, so a changed grade at four weeks is not available to be seen and anyone offering it is selling. A reasonable tutor will tell you at week four what they have found and what they are now working on, and that is the right deliverable for the stage.

At one term, it should be legible in the written work. A justification that argues rather than asserts. A solution another person could read without the student in the room. A model with a stated limitation. The student attempting a question whose topic they cannot immediately name. If the tutor's opening plan named three targets, two should be visibly different by the end of a term and the third needs an explanation. This is the point to decide whether to continue, and it is entirely reasonable to change tutor here rather than drift into a second term out of politeness.

Across a full year and an assessment cycle, the measure is independence. The student should need the tutor for fewer things: bringing their own problems, working for several days on something without rescue, writing up without being prompted on structure. If the Tuesday session has become a supervised homework hour, the arrangement has stopped doing what you bought even if the reports look fine. Ask the tutor once a term what the student can now do without them. A tutor who cannot answer that concretely is not tracking the right thing.

We cannot guarantee grades, and a tutor who promises a specific result is telling you something nobody is able to know. Too much depends on the other six days of the week, on which task lands in which week, and on how a particular student responds to a particular question on a particular morning. What a tutor is accountable for is the accuracy of the diagnosis, whether the right work is being done, and whether the student is becoming more independent. If a tutor is not working out, tell us what specifically is wrong and we arrange a replacement from the same zone, with no charge for the change and no requirement to explain yourself at length.

One term: justification, readable working, a stated limitation
One year: fewer things need the tutor, not the same list

sections.heading: Booking a first home session in Mumbai
paragraphs: Three things prepared in advance make the first session worth its hour. One piece of work the student found easy and one they found hard, which together say more than a term's marks. Any investigation task the school has returned with comments, because the comments on an investigation describe the thinking rather than the arithmetic. And a short, honest answer from the student to one question: when a maths problem does not tell you what to do, what do you do? Ask it without correcting the answer.

The session itself will not look like teaching and you should expect that. A tutor doing this properly spends most of the hour watching, with one or two questions set and a lot of waiting. They will probably go back a year or two in the content to check whether anything was learned as a procedure rather than understood, because that is where strong students hide their one real gap. The student may find it tiring and slightly unfamiliar, and may say afterwards that they did not learn anything, which is usually what a good diagnostic hour feels like from the inside.

Afterwards you get a short written plan: what the student can already do unaided, where the ceiling actually is, what the tutor will work on for the next six weeks, and what you should expect to see by the end of that. If the plan touches on route or on the school's own assessment, it is written as evidence for your conversation with the MYP coordinator and not as a recommendation to act on alone. For MYP subject groups home classes Mumbai families book mid-year, that document is the thing most worth keeping.

To start, send us the year group, the school, the current route and the slots that genuinely work, weekend mornings included. We come back with two or three names from your zone, what each has taught and how each would make a finished topic hard again. You speak to them, pick one, and book a single diagnostic session before committing to a term. If none of them are right, tell us and we look again, which is a normal part of this and not an awkward request.

Ask the student what they do when a problem gives no method

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child needs stretching rather than remedial help?
faqs.answer: Set one genuinely hard question with no method attached and watch the first two minutes. A student who needs stretching will argue with the problem, try something, and be annoyed when it resists them. A student who needs a gap repaired will wait, ask which topic it is from, or apply a method from somewhere else. The two look identical in homework behaviour, which is why marks alone mislead so many families. A tutor should be able to tell you which it is after two or three sessions, with the work in front of them and the reasoning written down.

faqs.question: What does a stretch session at home actually look like?
faqs.answer: Quieter than you expect. The tutor sets a problem in a topic the student has already covered, with no signposted method, and then stops talking. The student works, gets stuck, tries something else, and the tutor intervenes only to ask what has been tried. Much of the hour is the student writing. The last stretch is usually spent on the write-up: turning a correct answer into something another reader could follow. If you listen from the next room and hear the tutor explaining for most of the hour, the session is not doing what you booked it for.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor come twice a week for evening slots in Bandra or Andheri?
faqs.answer: Yes, but for stretch work once a week is usually the better buy. Twice-weekly suits repair work, where frequency closes gaps. Depth work needs days in between for the student to sit with a problem and get nowhere, which is where the learning happens. On logistics, both areas are well served: a tutor living in Khar, Santacruz or Bandra holds a 7pm Bandra slot comfortably, while Andheri West is easier from Oshiwara or Jogeshwari than from across the Western Express Highway at the evening peak. We match within the band rather than across it.

faqs.question: Our flat is small. Where should home classes happen?
faqs.answer: A dining table in a shared room works better than a bedroom, for younger MYP students especially. What matters is a hard surface big enough for two sheets of A4 side by side, decent light, a chair at the right height, and the television off rather than muted. A door that stays open is good practice. Mumbai flats in the island city and the older western suburbs are frequently tight, and no tutor worth booking will comment on the size of your home. Clearing the table ten minutes before the tutor arrives saves more session time than most families expect.

faqs.question: My child says MYP maths is boring. Is a tutor the right answer?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and sometimes it is the wrong purchase entirely. If boredom means the work is too easy, a tutor who brings depth is exactly right and will change things within a few weeks. If boredom means the student does not see why any of it matters, a tutor may help less than a reason: a problem from something they already care about, or a project. And occasionally a student says boring because it is a safer word than hard. Test with one difficult question before spending a term's fees on an assumption about which it is.

faqs.question: Should we do olympiad or competition maths instead?
faqs.answer: It can be excellent, and it is a different thing from what the MYP Extended route assesses. Competition problems build exactly the habit of starting an unfamiliar question, which is the single most useful habit for Criterion B work, so the overlap is real. What competition work does not build is the written communication and the real-world modelling the MYP criteria ask for. If the student enjoys it, run it alongside rather than instead, and keep some of the tutor's time for the write-up skills that competitions never test and the school's assessment always does.

faqs.question: What do home tuition fees depend on for Extended mathematics?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not print a price list that would be wrong across half the city. Level: MYP sits below Diploma Programme (DP) rates, and Extended a little above standard. Scarcity: tutors who can genuinely stretch a strong mathematician are the smallest group on any platform. Travel: a tutor crossing zones prices the journey in, which is one more reason to match locally. Session length and frequency. And experience with the programme rather than the content alone. IB tuition fees in Mumbai vary enough that the only sensible approach is asking each shortlisted tutor directly and comparing like for like.

faqs.question: Will stretching now help with DP mathematics later?
faqs.answer: The habits transfer; the specific content matters less than parents assume. A student who can start an unfamiliar problem, justify a generalisation and write mathematics another person can read is better prepared for Diploma Programme (DP) mathematics than one who has been pushed two chapters ahead. How your school links MYP routes to DP course choices is school policy and it differs between Mumbai schools, so ask the MYP coordinator what the current guidance says rather than relying on what another family was told two years ago. Pushing content early is the version that tends to disappoint.

faqs.question: Can the tutor mark my child's investigation task?
faqs.answer: A tutor can mark work the student has already written and explain what would make it stronger next time. A tutor may never write, draft or supply any part of work that will be submitted for assessment, including an investigation task or any section of the Year 5 personal project. Where the line sits for your school is set out in its own academic honesty guidance, and that document is the one to follow rather than anybody's general advice. If a tutor offers help that sounds like producing the work, end the arrangement. The consequences of accepting fall on the student.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not stretching my child enough?
faqs.answer: Say so in week three, not in month three. The usual symptom is that sessions have quietly become a review of school homework, which is comfortable for everyone and achieves nothing you were paying for. Raise it directly with the tutor first; many will reset the approach immediately once they know what you actually want, because stretch work is harder to prepare and some default to support unless asked. If nothing changes within two sessions, tell us and we replace them from the same zone at no charge. Most families wait far too long out of politeness.

faqs.question: We are in Kharghar. Can a tutor commute for a weekend morning session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and weekend mornings are the most reliable slot in Navi Mumbai. Kharghar is matched with tutors from Kharghar, Belapur, Nerul, Vashi or Panvel, connected by Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, which makes a Saturday or Sunday session straightforward. The Atal Setu has made a tutor from the island city possible for weekend work where a weekday evening crossing still rarely survives a full term. A longer weekend session at home plus a short online review midweek is the arrangement that holds best for families this side of the creek.

paragraphs: An IB MYP extended mathematics online tutor in Mumbai is matched from the work, not from a list. That line matters more than the profile does. A student who finishes a class exercise in half the time needs a different teacher from one who needs the chapter again, and on an enquiry form the two requests look identical. We ask for marked work because it shows the thing a parent usually cannot describe from the outside: whether the method is written down at all, whether the student skips the steps a marker has to see, and whether the slips are careless or structural. A tutor who is only confident teaching content is the wrong match for this request. We shortlist people who are comfortable setting a problem they have not pre-solved and then sitting through the silence while a thirteen-year-old works on it.

Shortlists stay deliberately small. Three profiles is a decision a parent can make in one evening; eight is a research project nobody finishes. The trial session is paid and it is real teaching, not a sales call. sections.heading: Where extended mathematics sits in the IB Middle Years Programme in Mumbai
paragraphs: The IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs across Years 1 to 5, and in the later years many Mumbai schools offer mathematics along two routes: a standard route and an extended route that carries additional content and asks for more abstraction. Which route a student follows is decided by the school together with the family, usually on the evidence of classwork and teacher judgement. IB Gram has no part in that conversation and no standing to second-guess it. If you are still weighing the choice, the person to ask is the school's MYP coordinator or the mathematics teacher who marks the work, not a tutoring platform.

What a tutor can do is make the extended route survivable once it has been chosen. Extended mathematics is not the standard course with extra homework attached. It asks a student to hold more structure in their head at once, to generalise from cases rather than follow a worked pattern, and to write an argument a reader can follow. Plenty of students who answer correctly and fast find the writing side of that genuinely unfamiliar, because nothing in the earlier years required it of them.

The route also feeds forward. Schools in Mumbai that run both the MYP and the Diploma Programme (DP) often point extended mathematics students towards Higher Level (HL) mathematics later, which is a reason the middle years are worth getting right rather than coasting through. Nothing is fixed by it, and students move between routes and levels all the time, but the habits built in MYP 4 and MYP 5 are the ones a DP teacher will assume are already there. Current structure for any year should come from the live subject guide and the school, because the IB revises its guides on its own cycle.

For a family who wants one tutor across more than mathematics, we also list a MYP subject groups tutor in Mumbai, and some parents ask for MYP subject groups home classes Mumbai wide, meaning a single tutor covering two or three subject groups in one visit. That works better in the earlier years than in MYP 5, when the subjects start pulling apart.

sections.heading: The eight MYP subject groups, and the one criterion that exposes a quick student
paragraphs: The IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) is built from eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, physical and health education, and design. Mathematics is one of those eight, and in Year 5 it sits alongside the personal project, the long independent piece a student plans, carries out and reflects on with a supervisor at school. Our internal listing label for this service reads MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai, which is clumsy English but describes exactly what is on offer.

Mathematics in the MYP is assessed against four criteria, usually summarised as knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. We are not going to quote band descriptors or mark boundaries here, because they change and your school's copy is the one that counts. The useful point for this page is narrower: of those four, investigating patterns is the one that most reliably catches out a student who works quickly.

Investigating patterns asks a student to try cases, notice a relationship, state a general rule and then justify why it holds. A fast student often sees the rule two cases in and writes it down with nothing in front of it. On paper that looks like a lucky guess, because the examiner has no access to the thinking that produced it. The same student will then describe the task as easy and the mark as unfair, and both statements are honest from where they are sitting.

Communicating has the same shape. Notation, a labelled diagram, a line of reasoning that a reader who was not in the room can follow: none of that is natural to someone who has always been able to hold the whole problem in their head. Most of what a good tutor does on this route is slow the hand down to the speed of the argument. Criterion-by-criterion marking in detail belongs on our general MYP page; here the focus stays on how these habits are built over a video call.

Home tuition remains the lead service and we match it inside your corridor; online simply removes the corridor from the equation.

Distances there are short and the clock is not: a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba loses the evening to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals, which is why island families are matched within the island or moved online. sections.heading: What the Mumbai school calendar does to an extended mathematics student
paragraphs: Mumbai's IB schools mostly run a June start, which means the first assessments land while the monsoon is still closing roads and the family is still working out the year's rhythm. Families we work with attend Oberoi International School in Goregaon East, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo and JBCN International School, Chembur, among many others. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools, nor with the International Baccalaureate organisation; we name them only because their calendars are what actually shape a tutoring plan.

The pressure points are predictable once you have seen a few years of them. The weeks before the first interim report in the autumn term are when a parent discovers that strong answers have been scoring moderately, because that report is often the first time criterion-level feedback arrives in writing. For MYP 5 students, the personal project overlaps with the heaviest mathematics content of the year, and the project is the one that eats weekends. Then there is the long unit assessment stretch in the second half of the year, where extended topics arrive faster than they did in MYP 3.

Those dates are the reason we tell families to start a tutor in a quiet month rather than a loud one. A tutor who begins in the week of an assessment becomes a revision service, and a revision service cannot change how a student writes mathematics. Six weeks earlier, the same tutor can rebuild the habit of showing work before anything is riding on it. Mumbai's travel reality makes this worse than it has to be: a weekday evening slot in Thane or Navi Mumbai that works in August may be unworkable in November once the traffic thickens, which is one more argument for an online slot as the backup.

Where a family does want someone in the room, we list an IB home tutor in Mumbai alongside the online options, and plenty of households run both. Ask the school for its assessment calendar in the first month of the year. It is the single most useful document for planning IB home tuition in Mumbai, and almost nobody requests it.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online classes, or both for extended mathematics?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the service most Mumbai parents actually want, and for good reason: a tutor in the room sees the page, the posture and the moment attention goes. An extended mathematics home tutor can reach across, point at the line where the argument breaks, and set a fresh problem on the spot with nothing mediating it. For a younger MYP student who is easily pulled away by a phone, home classes solve a problem that no software solves. The cost is geography. A specialist in extended mathematics who lives in Vile Parle cannot hold a 7pm Kharghar slot through a full term, and the slot that collapses in November was never really available.

An IB MYP extended mathematics online tutor in Mumbai trades that physical presence for reach and for consistency. You get the person who knows the extended route rather than the person who lives nearby, and the session happens whether or not the Eastern Express Highway is moving. Over video the tutor's job changes shape: everything has to be made visible on purpose, because nothing is visible by accident. A shared whiteboard, a document camera or even a phone propped over the notebook, and a rule that the working goes on the screen before the answer is spoken.

Hybrid is what most families settle into without planning it. One home session a week for the longer, messier work, and one shorter online session mid-week for a problem set and a check. We also list an IB online tutor in Mumbai for families who want the convenience without the travel question at all, and an IB private tutor Mumbai parents book for one-to-one work in either mode. The honest version of this choice is that mode matters less than the tutor's willingness to make a quick student slow down.

There is a point where a room genuinely beats a screen, and it is worth naming. If your child will not write unless someone is physically beside them, if the household has no quiet corner at the hour the session falls, or if the connection drops often enough that a twenty-minute problem becomes three attempts, book home tuition and stop optimising. Video is a tool, not a principle.

sections.heading: What IB Gram checks before an online or home tutor starts in Mumbai
paragraphs: Verification here means a few specific, boring checks rather than a badge. We confirm identity against a government photo document. We confirm the degree or teaching qualification a tutor claims, from the certificate rather than from the profile text. Where a tutor says they have taught the IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) or examined for it, we ask which school or which board relationship, and we ask for a contactable reference who can confirm the subject and the years involved. Claims we cannot substantiate come off the profile, which is why some profiles read more thinly than a tutor would like.

For mathematics specifically we add one practical step: the tutor marks a sample piece of student work and tells us what they would do in the first three sessions. That single task separates people who can teach extended mathematics from people who can do extended mathematics. A tutor who reads a correct-but-unjustified answer and marks it correct is not ready for this route, however strong their own degree is.

Then there is the half of verification a platform cannot do for you. Sit in on one session, or leave the door open for the first ten minutes of an online one, and listen for whether the tutor is asking or telling. Ask for the written plan after the trial and read it for specifics: a plan that names a criterion and a habit is real, a plan that promises confidence is not. Ask what happens in the session when your child gets something wrong, because the answer reveals the method. And be wary of anyone who promises a specific grade by a specific term. We do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor can.

If something feels off after two sessions, you do not need a reason you can argue. Write a line, and we will send fresh profiles. A rematch in week two costs far less than a tutor who stays until March out of politeness.

sections.heading: Why can't a tutor see a quick student's thinking on video?
paragraphs: Because a quick student answers before the thinking is visible, and on a screen the tutor loses the one thing a classroom gives them for free: the sideways glance at the page. In a room you watch the pencil. On video you hear a correct answer eleven seconds after the question and have no idea whether it came from a general argument, a remembered case or a good guess. This is the central problem of being an IB MYP extended mathematics online tutor in Mumbai for a capable younger student, and it has practical fixes rather than clever ones.

The first fix is a silent attempt block. The tutor sets a problem, the student turns the camera onto the notebook, and for several minutes nobody speaks. The tutor watches the writing appear and says nothing, including when a wrong turn starts. That silence is uncomfortable for everyone and it is where the diagnosis lives: you see whether the student starts with cases or with a formula, whether the next line follows from the last one, and where the hand stops. A session built on question-and-answer ping-pong never produces that information, because the tutor fills every gap before the student can.

The second fix is setting harder problems live instead of explaining harder problems. If the tutor works through a demanding example on the shared board, the student watches a competent adult be competent and learns very little. If the tutor hands over a problem one notch above comfortable and then stays quiet, the student produces something, and what they produce is the lesson. The third fix is the real check: the student teaches the method back, out loud, with the board shared, while the tutor plays the reader who was not there. Nothing exposes an unjustified generalisation faster than being asked to explain it to someone who refuses to fill in the gaps.

Keeping a thirteen- or fourteen-year-old with you while the work is deliberately difficult is its own skill. Short blocks, a visible finish line for the session, problems with a genuine hook rather than decorative real-world framing, and a tutor who says plainly that this question is meant to be hard and that getting stuck is the point. Praise aimed at the working rather than at the answer changes behaviour within a few weeks. And the honest limit: when the connection is unreliable, when the household is loud at that hour, or when the student simply will not write unless someone is sitting beside them, a room beats a screen and a home tutor is the better booking.

sections.heading: How quickly should extended mathematics work actually improve?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see a change in the page, not in the marks. The working gets longer, the diagrams get labelled, and a problem that used to produce one line now produces six. Parents often read this as the tutor being slow, because the score on the next unit test may not have moved at all. It usually has not. Four sessions is enough to change a habit in the room and not enough to change how a student performs under time pressure with a marker they have never met.

At one term the marks start to follow, and the pattern is uneven. Investigating patterns and communicating tend to move first, because they respond to the habit the tutor has been building. Knowing and understanding sometimes dips briefly, which sounds alarming and usually is not: a student who has started writing full arguments is spending time they used to spend finishing. Expect the teacher's written comments to change before the grades do, and ask to see them. One exam cycle is the first honest test of whether the work holds when nobody is prompting.

Where an IB MYP extended mathematics online tutor in Mumbai genuinely cannot help is also worth saying. Tutoring does not fix a timetable with no room in it, a student who has decided the subject is not for them, or a gap in the earlier years that needs rebuilding rather than stretching. It will not compress two terms of content into a fortnight before an assessment. And it will not change a school's route decision, which stays with the school and the family.

We do not guarantee grades, and anyone in this business who does is selling something other than teaching. What we will do is tell you at the end of the first month whether the match is working, in writing, including when the answer is that it is not. A tutor who says a student is doing fine every week for a term is not giving you information. Progress that is real shows up in the notebook, and the notebook is the thing to ask for.

sections.heading: Starting with an extended mathematics home tutor or online slot in Mumbai
paragraphs: Three things make the first session useful instead of introductory. Put together the last two marked pieces of mathematics, including the teacher's comments, even if they are unflattering. Write one sentence on what prompted the search, because 'the marks are fine but the feedback says the reasoning is missing' sends us somewhere completely different from 'the work has stopped being interesting'. And decide the slot before you decide the mode, because a brilliant tutor at an hour your household cannot hold is not a brilliant tutor.

The first session is a diagnosis, and it should feel like it. The tutor sets work rather than explaining the course, watches how it is produced, pushes one problem past comfortable to see where the method stops, and spends the last few minutes asking the student to teach a piece of it back. There is no syllabus tour. Afterwards you receive a short written note: the two skills to build, the habit to break, and what the next three sessions will do. If you want an IB tutor Mumbai parents can also meet in person, say so and we will shortlist for the room instead of the screen.

Set up for an online session in advance if that is the mode you choose. A table rather than a bed, the notebook within camera reach, headphones, and the phone in another room for the hour. faqs.question: Is an online tutor enough for extended mathematics, or should we book home tuition instead?
faqs.answer: Either works; the deciding factor is your child, not the subject. An IB MYP extended mathematics online tutor in Mumbai reaches a genuine specialist in the extended route and runs whatever the traffic is doing, which matters for a narrow subject with few local teachers. A home tutor sees the page and the attention directly, which matters more for a younger student who will not write unless someone is beside them. Many families run both: a longer home session weekly plus a short online problem-set check mid-week. Start with whichever you can hold every week, and change mode after a month if the notebook says you should.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Powai for an evening slot instead of teaching online?
faqs.answer: Yes, and Powai is one of the areas where we match home tutors regularly. The practical constraint is the road: Powai has no station of its own, so a tutor arrives by car or auto from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar along JVLR, and a 6.30pm arrival is a different commitment from a 4.30pm one. We ask tutors to commit to a slot they can actually hold through November, not just in August. Tell us your society's visitor protocol when you book, because a tutor who has to be cleared at the gate every week loses the first ten minutes of each session.

faqs.question: My child answers correctly but writes almost nothing down. Can that be fixed over video?
faqs.answer: Yes, and video has one advantage here: it forces the issue. The tutor sets a problem, the camera points at the notebook, and nobody speaks until the working appears. There is nowhere to hide an unwritten method, because the tutor literally cannot see an answer that was never written. The habit usually shifts within four to six weeks, first in the tutor's session and later in class. Expect the notebook to change before the marks do. Praise aimed at the working rather than the answer is what makes it stick, and most of that has to happen at home too.

faqs.question: How does a tutor set harder problems without just confusing a 13-year-old?
faqs.answer: By going one notch above comfortable, not five, and by saying out loud that the question is meant to be hard. The tutor sets a problem they have not pre-solved, stays quiet while the student attempts it, and intervenes only when the attempt has genuinely stalled rather than when it has slowed. Getting stuck is the intended experience on the extended route, and a student who has never been stuck has not yet been taught anything useful about mathematics. What breaks a younger student is not difficulty; it is difficulty with no visible finish line and no acknowledgement that it is difficult.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Session rates are set by each tutor, and we will not quote a figure that would be wrong for your case. What moves the number is consistent: the programme and level, how scarce the subject specialism is, session length and frequency, and for in-person work the travel distance and the hour of day. Extended mathematics at MYP 4 and 5 sits in a narrower pool than general mathematics, which affects availability more than anything else. Online sessions remove travel from the calculation entirely, which is often the single largest difference between an online and a home quote for the same tutor.

faqs.question: Do we need a parent at home during an online session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but presence in the house helps for a younger MYP student. What is worth doing is being around for the first ten minutes of the first few sessions, with the door open, to hear whether the tutor is asking or telling. After that, the useful parental job is logistical: the phone somewhere else, a table rather than a bed, and the notebook within camera reach. Hovering through every session tends to make a thirteen-year-old perform rather than think. Read the tutor's written note each week instead; it tells you more than listening in does.

faqs.question: What if there is no visible progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Then something is wrong with the match or the plan, and you should say so rather than wait. At four weeks the marks may legitimately not have moved, but the notebook should have: longer working, labelled diagrams, a method written before the answer. If the page looks identical to the page from week one, that is a real signal. Ask the tutor directly what has changed and what they are tracking. If the answer is vague, write us a line and we will send new profiles. A rematch in week five is far cheaper than a tutor who stays until March.

faqs.question: We live in Kharghar and most IB specialists seem to be in the Western Suburbs. Does that matter online?
faqs.answer: No, and this is where video earns its place. Over a screen a student in Kharghar or Panvel is matched to the same pool as a student in Khar West, with no reference to Palm Beach Road, the Atal Setu or the Harbour Line. For in-person work the geography is unavoidable: Navi Mumbai is matched node to node, so a Kharghar family gets a Kharghar, Belapur or Nerul tutor rather than someone commuting across the creek for a weekday evening. If you want a room, we will look locally. If you want the extended specialist, look online.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: You write one line and we start a new shortlist; you do not owe us an argument. No notice period applies and we do not ask you to persist through a trial month to prove the point. In practice most mismatches are about pace or manner rather than competence, and they show up inside three sessions. We will ask one question about what did not fit, because it makes the next shortlist better, and then send two or three fresh profiles. If a tutor has become unreliable about timing, tell us that too; it affects whether they stay listed.

sections.heading: How IB Gram shortlists an IB MYP extended mathematics tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: A request for an IB MYP extended mathematics tutor in Mumbai arrives with almost no information attached, so the first job is working out what is actually being asked. Two families send the same sentence and want opposite things. One has a Year 9 student at an International Baccalaureate (IB) school who finishes the set exercise in ten minutes and then goes quiet for the rest of the lesson. The other has a Year 10 student on the Extended route who gives mathematics three hours a night and still comes out of a task unsure what the question wanted. A shortlist built for the first family is close to useless for the second, which is why we ask before we send names.

The matching runs in four steps. 1. You tell us the year group, the school, which mathematics route the student is on now, and what made you start searching this week rather than last term. 2. We ask for two things: the most recently marked piece of mathematics, and whatever written guidance the school has given the family about routes. 3. We build a shortlist of two or three tutors from your own side of the city, each with Middle Years Programme (MYP) teaching behind them rather than board exam coaching alone. 4. You speak to each of them yourself, choose one, and treat the first session as a diagnosis rather than a lesson. Nothing in that sequence asks you to pay before you have spoken to a tutor and heard how they would work.

The zone rule matters more than it sounds. A tutor who agrees to cross the city twice a week for a 7pm slot will hold it for about a month and then start asking to move it to Sunday. Matching inside a corridor, Khar to Santacruz or Vashi to Nerul, is the difference between home tuition that survives a full term and home tuition that quietly falls apart in October when the assessment calendar tightens. We would rather hand you two names who live twenty minutes away than five who read well on paper and arrive at 7:25pm with an apology about the Western Express Highway.

What comes back to you after the first session is written rather than verbal: what the student can already do unaided, where the reasoning actually breaks, and what the tutor proposes to work on over the next six weeks. If the evidence suggests the student would be better served on the standard route, the document says so and gives the reasons. It does not make that call. Route placement belongs to the school, taken with the family, and a tutor who has met your child twice is not in a position to overrule a department that has taught them for two years.

sections.heading: Standard or Extended: how the MYP mathematics route is set
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs across Years 1 to 5 and is built from eight subject groups, of which mathematics is one. In the later years of the programme most schools run mathematics on two routes, usually called standard and extended. Extended is not a separate subject with a separate syllabus; it is the same framework carried further, with additional content and a heavier expectation that the student supplies the reasoning rather than receiving it. A student on either route is still doing MYP mathematics and is still assessed against the same four criteria.

Placement on a route is a decision the school makes, normally in discussion with the family, using evidence the school holds: classwork, assessed tasks, how a student handles unfamiliar questions, and the teacher's read on what the next two years will ask. It is a judgement about fit for the work ahead, not a ranking and not a statement about what a child is capable of. Schools in Mumbai run the process on different timetables. Some set routes near the start of Year 4, some part way through, some review at the end of the year and move students in both directions. If you do not know how your school does it, that question belongs to the MYP coordinator and is worth asking in writing.

Parents also ask what Extended means for the Diploma Programme (DP) later. There is a real relationship between the mathematics a student does in MYP and the DP mathematics course they go on to, but the way a particular school handles that link is a school policy, not a universal rule, and it changes. Do not take a WhatsApp group's version of it. Ask the coordinator what the school's current progression guidance says, and ask what happens if the student changes route mid-programme. The answer varies enough between Mumbai schools that borrowing another family's answer is a genuine risk.

This is where an MYP subject groups tutor in Mumbai is useful before they are useful as a teacher. A tutor who has taught the programme can look at a marked task and tell you what the comments are describing: whether the student is losing ground on content they have not met, or on the step where the question stops telling them what to do. Those two problems look identical on a report and need completely different work. The tutor's reading is evidence you can take into a conversation with the school, which is a far better use of it than trying to settle the route question at your dining table.

sections.heading: What does Extended mathematics actually add to the MYP course?
paragraphs: Extended mathematics adds further content within the same branches and asks for noticeably more of the thinking to come from the student. The branches do not change: number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, and statistics and probability. What changes is how far into each one the course travels, and how often a question arrives without an obvious method attached to it. That second change is the one families underestimate.

MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria, and each of them asks for something different. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is the one that looks most like a conventional maths test: can the student select and apply the right procedure, including in a situation they have not seen set out that way before. Criterion B, investigating patterns, starts where most textbook exercises stop. A task might give four figures in a growing sequence. Predicting the fifth is the easy part. The criterion wants a general rule, tested against cases the student chooses, and then justified: an argument for why the rule must hold for every figure, not merely for the four that were drawn. Students who are quick at arithmetic often lose ground here first, because speed is not the skill being measured.

Criterion C, communicating, is about whether a reader can follow the mathematics. Correct notation, a line of working that does not jump three steps, a diagram labelled well enough to be read without the student standing next to it, and a result stated in the form the question asked for. Criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, asks the student to build a model of a situation, use it, and then say honestly what the model gets wrong and how far the answer can be trusted. The reflection is part of the task, not decoration at the end of it.

How your school reports against those criteria, and what the current published descriptors say, is something to read in the school's own documentation rather than take from a tutoring website. Subject guides are revised on the organisation's own cycle, and the version that applies is the one your child's teacher is working from. The Year 5 personal project sits alongside all of this as a separate piece of work with its own requirements; it is worth knowing when your school schedules it, because it competes for the same evenings as mathematics.

sections.heading: Which months put MYP mathematics pressure on Mumbai families?
paragraphs: The pressure points in Mumbai are late October through November, and February through the end of the school year. International schools here mostly open in June and run two semesters, so the first cluster of assessed mathematics tasks lands once the term has settled and the monsoon has stopped rearranging the week. The second and heavier cluster falls in the closing months, when end-of-year assessment, the Year 5 personal project at schools that schedule it late, and the start of route conversations all arrive together.

Families searching for support in Mumbai come from across the city's IB and IGCSE schools: Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School on JVLR in Goregaon East, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, the JBCN International School campuses at Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, Bombay International School at Babulnath, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. Naming them is local context and nothing more. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school listed here, nor with the International Baccalaureate organisation.

Knowing the school matters because the calendars genuinely differ. A Year 4 student at a Juhu school may meet their first substantial investigation task weeks before a cousin at a Thane school meets theirs, and the two families will reach the same conclusion about needing help at different times. Schools also vary in how much mathematics they set over the Diwali break and how they handle the gap around the winter holidays, which is the period when a standing home tuition slot most often lapses and is hardest to restart.

The practical advice is to start earlier than feels necessary. A tutor booked in July has time to spend the first month on diagnosis and on the reasoning habits that Criterion B rewards. A tutor booked in the second week of November is being asked to produce a result before a deadline that is already set, which is the hardest possible brief and the one most likely to end in disappointment on both sides. If you are reading this in June or July, that is the useful month to act in.

sections.heading: Home tutor, online tutor or hybrid for Extended mathematics in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the first choice for Extended mathematics and it is what most Mumbai families book. The reason is specific to this course rather than general. Criterion C work is written work, and a tutor sitting beside a student can see the page as it is being produced: the step that was skipped, the notation that drifted, the diagram that was never labelled. An IB home tutor in Mumbai can also read the room in a way video cannot, which matters when a capable student has started to hide difficulty behind speed. Most families run one or two sessions a week of sixty to ninety minutes, at the same time each week, with the student's own desk and their own marked work to hand.

Online suits a narrower set of situations and it suits them well. If the student needs a tutor with a particular depth in the subject and nobody in your corridor has it, an IB online tutor in Mumbai removes the travel constraint entirely. Online also holds up better across a holiday, when families leave the city but want the weekly rhythm kept, and it makes a short mid-week check before a deadline practical in a way a forty-minute drive never will. The honest trade-off is that written mathematics is harder to supervise over video, and a younger MYP student usually needs a parent within earshot for the first few sessions rather than a closed door.

Hybrid is what a good number of Mumbai families settle into after a term, and it is worth considering from the start rather than arriving at by accident. A longer in-person session at the weekend handles new material, investigation work and anything that needs the tutor to watch the student write. A shorter online session mid-week handles questions, a review of marked work and the push before a task is due. For a family in Kharghar or Kasarvadavali, where a tutor's weekday evening journey is the weak link in any arrangement, hybrid is often the only version that lasts.

Whichever mode you pick, the test is the same after six weeks: is the student attempting unfamiliar questions without being told how to start. An IB MYP extended mathematics tutor in Mumbai who is working will have made that happen in some small way. One who has turned the session into a supervised homework hour will not have, and the mode will not be the reason.

sections.heading: How a tutor is checked before they reach your Mumbai home
paragraphs: Every tutor on IB Gram is checked on identity, on qualification and on teaching history before they are shown to a family. Identity means a government photo identity document seen and recorded. Qualification means the actual degree certificate for the subject being taught, not a line on a profile. Teaching history means naming where they have taught, for how long, and at which programme level, with contactable references for at least one of those places. For an IB MYP extended mathematics tutor in Mumbai we also look for evidence of teaching the programme specifically, because a strong mathematics graduate who has only coached board exams will teach Criterion A content well and have no instinct at all for what Criterion B rewards.

There are checks we cannot do for you, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. We cannot verify how a tutor will get on with your particular child, whether they explain in a way that suits the way your child thinks, or whether they will stay patient in week nine when the same misconception comes back. Those come out in the first session and in the two weeks after it, which is exactly why the first session is diagnostic and why we expect you to speak to each shortlisted name before choosing. An IB private tutor Mumbai parents found through a building group may be excellent; the point is that you should still ask the same questions.

The questions worth asking are concrete. Which MYP years have you taught, and on which route? Show me how you would mark this piece of my child's work. What would you do in the first three sessions? How do you handle a task that is due on Friday? A tutor who answers those in specifics is telling you something real. Be wary of anyone who promises a specific grade, offers to improve results by a fixed amount, or is vague about where they have taught. Searches for IB tutors near me Mumbai will surface plenty of confident claims and very few checkable ones.

One boundary is absolute and it protects your child rather than us. A tutor may teach, explain, set practice and mark work the student has done. A tutor may never write, draft, partly draft or supply any portion of work that will be submitted for assessment, including an investigation task or any part of the personal project. If a tutor offers that, the right response is to end the arrangement and tell us, because the consequences of accepting fall on the student and not on the adult who offered.

sections.heading: The student placed on Extended for the wrong reason
paragraphs: This is the conversation IB Gram has most often on this particular search, and it is worth having openly. A student ends up on Extended mathematics because a parent wanted it, or because a sibling did it, or because a parent group treated the standard route as a closed door. The student then works considerably harder than their classmates for an outcome that is worse than the one the standard route would have produced, and nobody involved did anything unreasonable. The parent was trying to keep options open. The school agreed to a parental request rather than force a confrontation in Year 4. The student said nothing because they could see what was wanted. Three people acting in good faith produced a bad fit.

What it looks like in practice is distinctive once you have seen it. The student keeps up on content; they can do the procedures. They fall down where the question stops telling them what to do, and they fall down on time, because every task takes them a third longer than it should and the extra material means there is more of it. Marks drift down across a semester rather than dropping sharply. Mathematics starts occupying evenings that belonged to the other subject groups, and a language or a science that was previously comfortable starts slipping, which is usually the signal a parent notices first. The student is not behind and nothing is wrong with them. The workload is simply shaped for a different use of their time.

The honest position on the other side is that plenty of students on Extended are exactly where they should be and are being asked to work hard, which is not the same problem. The difference shows in what happens with an unfamiliar question. A student who is well placed will circle it, try something, get somewhere and need help finishing. A student who is poorly placed will stall at the start and wait, every time, however much content revision has been done. A tutor can tell you which pattern they are seeing after two or three sessions, with the work in front of them. Our listing line reads MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai, which is an unlovely phrase, and this diagnosis is the part of it that matters.

If the evidence points to a route change, the request goes to the school and the school decides, with you. Nobody searching for the best IB tutor in Mumbai should expect a tutor to carry that conversation for them, and no tutor should offer to. Take the marked work, take the tutor's written view, ask the MYP coordinator what the school's criteria are and what changing route would mean for the student's options later, and ask it early enough in the year to be acted on. Moving to the standard route is a decision about fit, not a verdict on your child, and a student who moves and then does well has lost nothing worth keeping.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one year
paragraphs: At four weeks, the honest marker is behavioural rather than numerical. The student starts an unfamiliar question instead of waiting to be shown. They write more down. They can say, when asked, what a question is actually testing. Marks may not have moved at all by week four and frequently have not, because the assessment calendar has not come round again. A parent who expects a changed grade in a month is measuring something that has not happened yet, and a tutor who promises one is telling you what you want to hear.

At one term, you should see it in the marked work. Working that a reader can follow without the student present. A generalisation that is tested and argued for rather than asserted. A model with its limitations stated. If the tutor's six-week plan named three things to fix, two of them should be visibly better by now and the third should have a reason attached if it is not. This is also the point at which it is fair to ask whether the fit is right, and to change tutor if the answer is no.

At one year, the question is whether the student has become more independent or more dependent. A good arrangement ends up needing less: longer gaps between sessions, the student bringing their own questions, the tutor spending more time on investigation work and less on last night's homework. An arrangement that has quietly become a supervised homework hour every Tuesday can look fine on a report and has stopped doing the thing you are paying for. Ask the tutor directly, once a term, what the student can now do unsupervised that they could not do before.

IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor will. Too much sits outside anyone's control: how the student uses the other six days, what else the school year throws at them, how a particular task lands on a particular week. What a good tutor controls is the quality of the diagnosis, whether the right thing is being worked on, and whether the student is getting better at thinking rather than better at being helped. If a tutor is not working out, tell us: we will ask what specifically is not working, and arrange a replacement from the same zone without charging a fee for the change.

One term: working is followable and generalisations are justified
One year: the student needs the tutor less, not the same amount

sections.heading: Booking home classes for MYP mathematics in Mumbai
paragraphs: Three things make the first session useful and all of them are already in your house. The most recently marked piece of mathematics, ideally an investigation task rather than a topic test, because the teacher's comments on an investigation say far more about where the reasoning breaks. Any written route guidance the school has given, even a paragraph in a report. And ten minutes of the student's own account of what they find hard, taken without a parent correcting them, which is frequently the most accurate document in the file.

The session itself is not a lesson. A tutor should spend most of it watching the student work rather than talking: setting a question with no signposted method, waiting through the silence, and seeing what the student does with it. They will usually also go back two years in the content, because a gap in Year 7 algebra explains an awful lot of Year 10 difficulty and is quick to close once it has been found. Expect the student to come out of it slightly tired and slightly surprised. For MYP subject groups home classes Mumbai families book in the middle of a term, that first hour is the part that pays for itself.

What you receive afterwards is a short written plan: what the student can do, what is actually going wrong, what the tutor will work on for six weeks, and what you should see at the end of them. If the plan includes a view on whether the route is right, it will be written as evidence for your conversation with the school rather than as a recommendation to act on alone. You can take that document to the MYP coordinator exactly as it is.

To start, send the year group, the school, the current route, your area and the slots that genuinely work on a weekday evening. We come back with two or three names from your zone, what each has taught, and what they would do first. You speak to them, pick one, and book a single diagnostic session before committing to anything longer. If none of them fit, say so and we will look again; that is a normal outcome and not a difficult conversation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between MYP standard and extended mathematics?
faqs.answer: Extended covers additional content within the same four branches and expects more of the reasoning to come from the student. Number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, and statistics and probability appear on both routes; Extended goes further into each and sets more questions that arrive without an obvious method attached. Both routes are assessed against the same four criteria. The practical difference families notice is time: the same evening produces less finished work on Extended, because thinking time is part of the task rather than an overhead. Your school's own documentation is the place to check how it reports the two routes.

faqs.question: The school has placed my child on Extended mathematics. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: It means the school, looking at classwork and assessed tasks, judged Extended a reasonable fit for the next stage of the programme. It is a decision about fit and workload, not a ranking of students and not a prediction. Schools in Mumbai run placement on different timetables and with different criteria, and many review it rather than fixing it for good. If you want to understand the reasoning, ask the MYP coordinator what evidence was used and whether the placement is reviewed. That conversation is far more useful than trying to infer the answer from a report comment.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get my child moved from Extended back to standard?
faqs.answer: No. Route changes are decided by the school, with the family, and a tutor has no standing in that process whatever they may suggest. What a tutor can do is produce evidence: marked work with a written analysis of where the difficulty actually sits, which is more useful in a meeting than a parent's impression. Take that to the MYP coordinator, ask what the school's criteria for a change are, and ask what it would mean for the student's options later, since the answer varies between Mumbai schools. Any tutor who offers to arrange a route change is overstating what they can do.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Powai or Chembur for an evening home tuition slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and both are well served, but the realistic slot differs. Powai has no station of its own, so a tutor arrives by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and a 6pm start on JVLR is optimistic where 7pm is dependable. Chembur is easier: the Harbour Line, the SCLR and the Eastern Freeway all feed it, and tutors living in Chembur, Govandi or Wadala can reach a flat there inside twenty minutes off-peak. We match within those corridors rather than bringing someone across the city, because a long weekday journey is the thing that breaks a standing slot by the second month.

faqs.question: What does a home tutor need from our building or society on the first visit?
faqs.answer: Usually a visitor entry at the gate and, in larger complexes, a name added to a standing visitor list so the tutor is not held up at the desk every week. Tell your security office that the same person will come at the same time weekly; most Mumbai societies handle this routinely once asked. Beyond access, the tutor needs a table, a chair, decent light and a door that can stay open. Sessions work best in a shared space rather than a bedroom, particularly for younger MYP students, and a parent being somewhere in the flat is good practice rather than a lack of trust.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: They depend on five things, and we will not quote a figure that would be wrong for half the city. Programme and level: MYP sits below Diploma Programme rates, and Extended usually sits a little above standard. Subject scarcity: mathematics at depth has fewer qualified teachers than most subjects. Travel: a tutor crossing a zone prices the journey in, which is a further reason to match locally. Session length and frequency: ninety minutes twice a week is not twice the hourly rate of once. Tutor experience, including whether they have taught the programme rather than only the content. Ask each shortlisted tutor directly and compare on the same basis.

faqs.question: Is online better than home classes for Extended mathematics?
faqs.answer: Not usually, for this subject, though it is genuinely better in some situations. Written mathematics is the thing being assessed, and a tutor sitting beside a student sees the working as it forms, including the steps that get skipped silently. Online wins when the depth you need is not available in your corridor, when the family is away from Mumbai, or when a short mid-week review before a deadline would otherwise mean a wasted drive. Many families end up hybrid: a longer weekend session in person for new material and investigation work, a shorter online session mid-week for questions and marked work.

faqs.question: How soon should we see progress in MYP mathematics?
faqs.answer: Expect behaviour to change in about four weeks and marks to follow a term later. Early signs are that the student starts an unfamiliar question instead of waiting, writes more working down, and can explain what a question is testing. Marks often have not moved at four weeks simply because nothing has been assessed. By the end of a term you should see it in the work: followable working, a generalisation that is argued rather than asserted, a model with its limits stated. If none of that has appeared after a full term, the arrangement needs changing rather than extending.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out. What happens?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them, with no fee for the change. We will ask what specifically is not working, because the answer decides what we look for next: a mismatch of pace, a tutor who explains in one register when the student needs another, or an arrangement that has drifted into supervised homework. Replacements come from the same zone so the slot survives the change. It is worth saying this early rather than at the end of a term; most families wait too long out of politeness, and a term lost to a poor fit is harder to recover than an awkward phone call.

faqs.question: Can the tutor help with my child's personal project or an assessed investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills, discuss the approach in general terms and mark work the student has already written. A tutor may never write, draft or supply any part of work that will be submitted for assessment, including an investigation task or any section of the Year 5 personal project. That line is not negotiable and it exists to protect the student, since the consequences of crossing it fall on the child. If a tutor offers to help in a way that sounds like producing the work, end the arrangement and tell us. The school's own guidance on acceptable support is the document to follow.

faqs.question: We live in Thane off Ghodbunder Road. Is an evening slot realistic?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor also lives in Thane. Ghodbunder Road sets the timetable here: Kasarvadavali is twenty minutes from Thane station off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, so a tutor coming from Mulund or Powai will struggle to hold a 6:30pm start through a full term. We match Thane families with Thane tutors, drawing on Pokhran Road, Majiwada and the Ghodbunder corridor, and keep Mulund as a second option only where the slot is later or at a weekend. A 7:30pm start is often more reliable than a 6:30pm one.

paragraphs: A request for an IB MYP French home tutor in Mumbai arrives with more useful detail than most parents expect to give. We ask for the year group inside the Middle Years Programme (MYP), the school, the suburb, and one specific thing that went wrong recently: a written task that came back with comments about audience, an oral where the student froze, a listening exercise where the recording ran away from her. That last detail does more matching work than the first three combined, because French at this level breaks down in different places for different students, and a tutor who is excellent at oral coaching is not automatically the right person for a child whose writing drifts out of register.

We then filter on three things in order. French teaching experience inside the International Baccalaureate (IB) framework comes first, because a tutor who has only ever taught French for a different examination system will coach vocabulary lists and conjugation drills rather than the task types the MYP actually sets. Travel feasibility comes second: a home tutor who has to cross the Bandra Worli Sea Link twice a week at 7pm will be cancelling by November, whatever was agreed in October. Availability in your real slot comes third, and we check it against the student's school timetable and bus timing rather than against a generic evening window.

sections.heading: Where MYP French sits between the PYP and the Diploma Programme
paragraphs: French in the Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs across Years 1 to 5, which in most Mumbai schools covers roughly Grade 6 to Grade 10. A student may arrive having met some French in the Primary Years Programme (PYP), or may be starting from nothing in Year 1 because the school introduces the language there, or may be switching across from Spanish or Hindi after a year of something else. All three are ordinary and none of them says anything about the child. The programme is built to take a complete beginner to a point where the Diploma Programme (DP) is a genuine option, and the route is deliberately gradual.

Schools place MYP language acquisition students in phases, and the phase a student sits in is decided by the school in conversation with the family. It is not something a tutor sets and it is not something IB Gram has any say in. What a French IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai families engage can usefully do is describe, in plain terms, what the work at the current phase is asking for and whether your child is producing it comfortably. If a phase change is being considered, that conversation belongs with the school's language coordinator, and a tutor's written observations about what the student can and cannot yet do are useful input to it.

Parents of Year 4 and Year 5 students usually have one eye on the Diploma Programme. French ab initio, French B at Standard Level (SL) and French B at Higher Level (HL) are different propositions, and the MYP years are where the door to the wider options stays open or quietly narrows. None of that needs settling in Year 2. It does mean that the accuracy work described further down this page matters more than it appears to matter at the time, because it is cumulative and it cannot be done in a hurry later.
