faqs.question: What does criterion A to D marking actually mean on my child's MYP report?
faqs.answer: It means your child was judged against published descriptions of what work at each level looks like, in four separate strands of the subject, rather than given a percentage. The labels differ by subject, so criterion B in Sciences asks something quite different from criterion B in Language and Literature. A child can sit at a strong level in one criterion and a weak one in another and come out looking average overall, which is why the overall figure is the least useful part of the report. Ask the subject teacher which single criterion they would target next, and start there.

faqs.question: Can an MYP home tutor reach our building before 5pm on a school day?
faqs.answer: Usually, provided the tutor is matched locally, which is exactly why we match inside the island. A tutor already teaching in Cumballa Hill, Tardeo or Peddar Road can be at a tower on Altamount Road minutes after finishing elsewhere, so an early slot is realistic. A tutor travelling from the Western Suburbs for a 4:30pm start is fighting the Haji Ali and Peddar Road signals and will begin cancelling by the second month. Early slots are the scarce ones here, so ask for one at the start rather than trying to move later.

faqs.question: Is Year 5 the right time to start thinking about Diploma Programme subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, and earlier than most families do. The useful work in Year 5 is not teaching Diploma content ahead of time but testing readiness: a timed closed-book task in the intended Higher Level subject, one unscaffolded extended piece of writing, and an algebra fluency check. Those three reveal more about whether Higher Level Mathematics or Higher Level Chemistry is realistic than a year of criterion levels will. They also make the subject selection conversation concrete rather than aspirational, which is the conversation most families later wish they had had properly.

faqs.question: Does the personal project need a tutor, and what help is allowed?
faqs.answer: It does not need one, and where a tutor helps most is at the beginning rather than the end. A tutor can press the student towards a goal that is achievable in the weeks available, teach them to keep a process journal that records decisions rather than listing activities, explain what each criterion is asking, and read a draft and point out where a claim has no evidence behind it. A tutor cannot pick the goal, make the product or write the report, and should refuse to. Your school's academic honesty policy sets the line and the supervisor enforces it.

faqs.question: My child gets strong MYP levels. Will that hold in the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Often, but not automatically, and the gap is in habits rather than ability. The Diploma Programme moves faster, scaffolds tasks less, and ends in timed papers written without notes, which is the skill the Middle Years Programme rehearses least. Students who have always worked from a structured task sheet have to learn to impose structure themselves. Mathematics is where the drop is most common, because strong criterion levels do not prove the algebraic fluency Higher Level assumes. Test for those three things in Year 5 and the first Diploma term is far less of a shock.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups do parents in Mumbai ask about most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and Sciences by a wide margin, then Language and Literature, then Language Acquisition. Mathematics requests are usually about the investigation criterion, where a child who calculates accurately has never been taught to generalise a pattern and justify it. Sciences requests are about method and evaluation rather than content. Language and Literature requests are almost always the same problem: a capable writer who summarises where the criterion asks for analysis. Language Acquisition is the group where the right tutor is most often not local, and where we most often suggest weekly online lessons instead.

faqs.question: How does society gate entry work for a tutor coming weekly to our tower?
faqs.answer: It is set up once as a recurring entry rather than a new visitor request every week. Towers on this stretch run close entry control, and a tutor improvising at the lobby desk while security phones upstairs loses a real slice of a short lesson, which matters more when the lesson is an hour with a twelve year old. So we confirm two things in advance: how your building clears a recurring visitor, and whether anything is needed from you at the gate each time. The tutor is then briefed on that building's procedure before the first visit.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Altamount Road depend on at MYP level?
faqs.answer: Subject group, year, tutor scarcity, travel and session length, and we will not print a figure because the honest range is too wide to be useful. MYP tuition generally sits below Diploma Higher Level tuition because more tutors can teach it, with Language Acquisition in a less commonly taught language the usual exception. Travel is a real component in South Mumbai, since a tutor crossing the city is charging for lost evening hours, which is another reason local matching costs less. Ask for a per session figure in writing before the first lesson, and ask what a cancellation costs.

faqs.question: Is online MYP tuition workable for a Year 2 or Year 3 student?
faqs.answer: Rarely as the main arrangement. A child of that age on a video call drifts quickly, and the tutor cannot see the notebook, the handwriting or the moment comprehension stopped. For Years 1 to 3 we push hard for lessons in the apartment with a parent in earshot. Online earns its place from Year 4 upwards, and particularly for short focused checks: twenty minutes on one marked task, or a personal project milestone. If distance makes online the only option for a younger child, keep the sessions short and sit nearby.

faqs.question: What should change after four weeks of MYP tuition?
faqs.answer: You should be able to name what the tutor is targeting, and so should your child. A reasonable four week report says which criterion is being worked on, what the child was doing that cost levels, what has already changed and what has not. What you should not expect is a moved criterion level, because descriptor boundaries are coarse and genuine improvement often sits inside one level before crossing it. If the only feedback after a month is that sessions are going well, press for specifics or consider a different tutor.

faqs.question: Should we hire one tutor for several subject groups or one for each?
faqs.answer: One tutor across two related groups can work well; one tutor across four does not. A tutor comfortable in Mathematics and Sciences, or in Language and Literature and Individuals and Societies, brings genuine transfer, especially on the approaches to learning skills that lift every subject at once. Beyond that pairing you are buying convenience at the cost of depth, and the criteria really are subject-specific. Where a family needs three groups covered, we would rather suggest two tutors and a lighter schedule than one person stretched across everything.

faqs.question: What happens if the MYP tutor turns out not to suit my child?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them, with no lock-in and no penalty. With younger students this comes up more often than at Diploma level, and the reason is usually rapport rather than competence, which is a legitimate reason to change and not worth being polite about for a whole term. What speeds up the second match is specificity: not turning up on time, not setting work, explaining in a way the child does not follow, or simply not getting on. Each of those points at a different replacement profile.

sections.heading: MYP Years 1 to 5 and the eight subject groups
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme runs across five years and eight subject groups: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. A student is assessed in each against criteria specific to that group, which is why a child can be a strong writer in Language and Literature and lose marks in Individuals and Societies for the same essay skill applied to different expectations.

The years matter as much as the groups. MYP Years 1 and 2 are where reading stamina, number fluency and the habit of explaining an answer are built, and a weakness here is cheap to fix and expensive to ignore. MYP Year 3 is where the work starts demanding independent investigation, and it is the year most parents first notice a problem. MYP Year 4 is where the gap between a student who can produce and a student who can only perform becomes visible. Year 5 adds the personal project on top of everything else.

Design and Arts deserve a specific mention because families routinely treat them as the subjects where marks are free. They are not. Design in particular is assessed on a documented process of inquiry, development, creation and evaluation, and a student who makes something good without documenting how loses marks that look arbitrary to a parent and are entirely predictable to a teacher. Several of the MYP subject groups tutor in Andheri East requests we receive are really requests for help with documentation habits.

This page stays inside the Middle Years Programme. The Diploma Programme and the International General Certificate of Secondary Education route have their own pages, and so do the individual Diploma subjects. We touch the Diploma only in the section on the transition, because that is the thing MYP parents in Andheri East ask about most and it belongs here rather than on a Diploma page.

sections.heading: What do criteria A to D actually measure?
paragraphs: Four different things, and the labels differ by subject group, which is the root of most parental confusion. In Mathematics the criteria run from knowing and understanding, through investigating patterns, to communicating and then applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student who can compute perfectly and cannot find or describe a general rule will lose consistently on the second and third of those while her first-criterion performance stays strong, and the reported grade will sit in the middle and explain nothing.

In the Sciences the criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The second and third are investigation skills, and they are where most science marks are lost in MYP: a method that does not control variables, a data table without units, a conclusion that restates the data rather than interpreting it. The fourth criterion asks about science in context and is often the one students treat as an afterthought, which is visible immediately in the mark.

In Language and Literature the criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. A student with excellent ideas and weak organisation scores badly on a criterion she could fix in three sessions, because essay structure is teachable in a way that literary insight is not. In Individuals and Societies, thinking critically is the criterion that separates a student who reports from one who argues, and it is reliably the lowest score on the sheet for capable students.

The practical move for a parent is to lay the criteria sheets for all the subjects side by side and look for a pattern. A student weak on communication in Mathematics, on processing and evaluating in Sciences and on organising in Language and Literature does not have three subject problems. She has one problem with structuring and expressing what she knows, and one tutor working on exactly that will move all three. That cross-subject reading is the most useful hour an IB MYP tutor in Andheri East spends, and the one Mumbai parents least often ask for.

sections.heading: Are MYP home classes better than online in Mumbai?
paragraphs: For this age group, clearly yes, and the reason is attention rather than content. A thirteen-year-old online drifts within fifteen minutes, and a tutor on a screen cannot tell the difference between thinking and a tab change. In the room, a tutor reads posture, hesitation and the moment a student stops following, and adjusts immediately. For MYP Years 1 to 3 especially, in-person teaching is not a preference, it is most of what you are paying for.

Home tuition has a second advantage that matters specifically in the Middle Years Programme. Much of MYP assessment is process work, which lives in folders, journals and half-finished drafts. A tutor in the room can ask to see the process journal, flip back three weeks, and notice that nothing has been recorded since the task was set. That is invisible online unless a student volunteers it, and a student who has not been keeping a journal does not volunteer it.

Online earns a role in two cases. A scarce subject group, where the right Language Acquisition or Design teacher may not be within reach at all, and a short review before a deadline where twenty minutes on a draft beats waiting until next week. An IB online tutor in Andheri East can do both well, provided the student is old enough to hold attention and a stylus tablet or document camera exists for anything involving diagrams or working.

Hybrid works for MYP Years 4 and 5, less so below that. The weekly session happens at home, with occasional online check-ins during project weeks. Declare the pattern at the start so an online week counts as a lesson rather than reading as a cancellation. Families running MYP subject groups home classes Andheri East for two children of different ages often keep the younger one entirely in person and allow the older one hybrid, which is the right split rather than a compromise.

sections.heading: The personal project in Year 5, from proposal to report
paragraphs: The personal project is the piece of MYP work that most reliably goes wrong, and it goes wrong early. A student chooses something she cannot sustain for months, or something so vague that no finished outcome is definable, and the whole thing then has to be rescued under time pressure in the same term as her other assessments. The strongest predictor of a good project is a narrow, honest goal set early, with success criteria the student wrote herself and can actually test against.

The process journal is the second failure point and the most avoidable. It is not a diary written up at the end. It is contemporaneous evidence of decisions, dead ends, sources and changes of direction, and it carries real weight in the assessment. A student who creates an impressive outcome with no documented process has thrown away marks that were far easier to earn than the outcome itself. The habit to build, from week one, is five minutes of recording after every working session.

The supervisor at school is the primary relationship and a tutor must not displace it. What a tutor usefully does is ask the questions a supervisor has not got time to ask weekly: is this goal still the goal, does the evidence support the claim you are making, what would you do differently and can you show me where you decided that. Asking questions is the whole of the appropriate help. A tutor who contributes content or writing is creating an academic honesty problem that follows the student forward.

The sequence we recommend is three or four short sessions spread across the project: one at goal setting, one at the mid-point to test whether the goal has quietly drifted, one on the journal before the report is drafted, and one on the report structure. That is a small engagement with a disproportionate effect, and it is worth booking by the start of the project rather than in the final fortnight, which is when most requests in Mumbai actually arrive. An IB MYP tutor in Andheri East asked to help in the last two weeks can do very little that is both useful and appropriate.

sections.heading: The MYP to Diploma Programme step, and how to prepare for it
paragraphs: This is what MYP parents actually worry about, and the worry is well founded. The Middle Years Programme assesses process, investigation and reflection against descriptors, with tasks spread through the year. The Diploma Programme assesses performance in timed examinations with internal assessments on fixed deadlines. A student who has done well in MYP by being thoughtful and well organised can find the Diploma sudden, not because the content is beyond her but because the register has changed.

Three things prepare a student properly and all three can be built in MYP Years 4 and 5. Algebraic and quantitative fluency, because the Diploma sciences and mathematics assume it and no longer teach it. Writing to a time limit, which MYP rarely demands and the Diploma demands constantly. And the habit of working from a syllabus rather than from a task sheet, which is the real shift: in the Diploma nobody tells you what is coming next, and a student has to be able to look ahead herself. Those three are what we push hardest in MYP home classes in Mumbai.

At four weeks of tuition, what you should see is a diagnosis rather than a grade change: she can investigate well and loses marks on communicating her findings, or he knows the science and never addresses the fourth criterion at all. By the end of a term, look for the lowest criterion on the sheet moving while the overall grade possibly does not, which is the normal and correct order of events. Ask for criterion-level feedback rather than a grade prediction.

The limits are honest ones. A tutor cannot change teacher-assessed criteria judgements and should not try. A tutor cannot write a personal project or an investigation, and heavy editing creates a problem that follows your child into the Diploma years. A tutor cannot make a fourteen-year-old keep a process journal. Where the real issue is organisation rather than understanding, more hours of IB home tuition in Andheri East will help less than a conversation with the school about structure and deadlines.

sections.heading: MYP Years 1 to 5: what changes as your child moves up
paragraphs: The programme runs five years and the demand changes shape rather than simply increasing. In Years 1 and 2, most children are learning how to work inside an inquiry structure: finding evidence, recording thinking, and producing something that shows a process rather than just an answer. Difficulty at this stage is almost never about content. It is about a child who can do the work and cannot yet show that they did it, which looks like underachievement on a criterion sheet and is really a skills gap.

Years 3 and 4 are where subject-specific demand arrives properly. Mathematics starts expecting algebraic fluency, the sciences start expecting investigation design, and language and literature starts expecting analysis rather than summary. This is the stretch where a gap left alone becomes structural, and it is also the stretch where parents are least likely to act, because there is no examination on the horizon to force the issue. Most of the MYP work we arrange is Years 3 and 4 for exactly this reason.

Year 5 is different again. Subject choices for the Diploma Programme (DP) are made during it, the personal project runs through it, and some schools enter students for external MYP assessment at the end while others do not, so the shape of the year depends on your school's decision. Ask the coordinator directly which route your child's cohort is on. An IB MYP tutor in Andheri West working with a Year 5 student should know the answer before planning a term.

This page is about the MYP specifically. The Diploma Programme and the Primary Years Programme have their own pages, and the Cambridge route has its own, because treating the MYP as a junior version of the DP is the commonest mistake made about it. It is a distinct programme with distinct assessment logic, and the tutoring it needs is not a watered-down version of DP tutoring.

sections.heading: The eight subject groups and the criteria behind each grade
paragraphs: Before any home tutor plans a term, the eight groups are worth knowing: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. Each one is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, and each criterion is marked in its own right against published descriptors. The subject grade comes from combining those criterion judgements, which is why a student can be strong in a subject and receive a middling grade: three criteria well met and one badly met averages to something that looks like general mediocrity and is nothing of the kind.

The criteria differ by group, which is the part parents rarely learn. In the Sciences they cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In Mathematics they cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Language and Literature they cover analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. A student who is excellent at mathematical technique and weak at communicating a method will lose consistently on one criterion across every unit, and no amount of extra content teaching will fix it.

That is the single most useful diagnostic insight available to an MYP parent. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown rather than the subject grade, across two or three units. The pattern is usually obvious: the same criterion, low, repeatedly. Design and the Arts have their own version of this, where students produce good outcomes and lose marks on the documentation of the process. Across the eight MYP subject groups the home classes Andheri West families book cluster in Mathematics, the Sciences and Language and Literature, and in each the recurring problem is a criterion rather than a topic.

Approaches to learning skills run across all eight groups: research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills. They are taught in context rather than as a separate subject, which means they are easy for a student to miss entirely. A tutor who works explicitly on self-management and research skills alongside the subject content is doing something the school may be doing only implicitly, and it is often the highest-value part of the work in Years 3 and 4.

sections.heading: Why does the MYP report card confuse Mumbai parents?
paragraphs: Because it reports against criteria and most parents are reading it as a percentage. A grade arrives with four criterion judgements behind it, and the comment often names a criterion by letter without explaining what that criterion asks for. A parent sees effort at home, a reasonable grade, and a comment that sounds like a complaint, and cannot connect the three. The information is all there; the translation is missing. The first useful conversation with the school is asking what the named criterion requires and what a stronger response to it would look like.

The second source of confusion is that criterion performance varies by task type rather than by topic. A student can meet a criterion well on a written report and badly on a presentation of the same material, because the criterion is about communication rather than about content. So a report that looks inconsistent often reflects the mix of task types in the term rather than a student blowing hot and cold.

Children in this area attend JBCN International School, Oshiwara, Billabong High International School and Ecole Mondiale World School, and each runs its own MYP unit calendar, assessment weeks and reporting cycle. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of those schools, their staff or their assessment arrangements. We name them because the unit plans and task sheets that drive the term come from the school, and a tutor working without them is working blind.

Two requests that repay the effort. Ask for the criterion breakdown across the last two or three units, not just the current grade, because the pattern is where the diagnosis lives. And ask the subject teacher what a top-band response to the weak criterion would contain for the next task specifically. Teachers answer specific questions specifically, and a tutor handed that answer can build a plan in one evening instead of spending three sessions reverse-engineering it.

Criterion performance varies by task type, not by topic
Ask what the named criterion requires and what a stronger answer looks like
Get the criterion breakdown across two or three units
Unit plans and task sheets come from the school, not from a syllabus

sections.heading: Home classes or online for a Year 8 student in Mumbai?
paragraphs: For this age group, in person, and the reason is attention rather than teaching quality. A thirteen-year-old in a room with a tutor stays on task. The same child on a call with a laptop finds a second tab within twenty minutes, and the tutor cannot see it. MYP home classes in Andheri West are the lead arrangement for Years 1 to 4 and we recommend them without much hedging, which is not true of our advice for DP students.

Online becomes reasonable from Year 5, when a student has more self-management and the work includes personal project supervision and extended writing that transfers well to a screen. It is also the right answer for Language Acquisition in a less commonly taught language, where the only good tutor may be nowhere near the Link Road, and for the short check-in sessions that keep a project moving between in-person meetings.

If online is used with a younger MYP student, the household has to do the enforcement a tutor cannot. A shared room with the door open, not a bedroom. A laptop on a table, not a phone. A parent within earshot for the first few sessions. An IB online tutor in Andheri West can be effective with a Year 7 or Year 8 child only when those conditions are actually met, and a tutor who sets them out on the first call is being realistic rather than difficult.

Hybrid works well in Year 5, with one in-person session for subject teaching and one short online session for personal project check-ins. It also covers the monsoon, turning a washed-out early-evening Juhu or Versova slot into a shorter call rather than a cancellation, which is worth agreeing in June. What does not work is an unplanned mixture: a child this age treats a format they cannot predict as optional.
bullets: Years 1 to 4: in person, because attention is the binding constraint
Online becomes workable from Year 5 with more self-management
Language Acquisition in a rarer language is the main online exception
Online with a younger child needs a shared room and no phone
Hybrid suits Year 5: teaching in person, project check-ins online

sections.heading: Checking a tutor has actually taught the MYP, not just the subject
paragraphs: This is the check that matters most before you hire an IB MYP tutor in Andheri West, because the MYP is where subject-qualified tutors most often come unstuck. We verify identity through government photo identification, subject qualification in the subject group itself, and MYP teaching experience evidenced specifically rather than inferred from general international school work. There is also a programme conversation, because somebody who can teach the content and cannot read a criterion descriptor will teach your child to produce work that scores below its quality.

Your own test takes two questions. Ask the candidate to name the four criteria in your child's subject group. A tutor who has taught the MYP knows them, in order, without looking. Then ask what a task-specific clarification is and what they do with one. The right answer involves reading it before planning the session, because it defines what each criterion means for that particular task. A candidate who talks about covering the syllabus instead has not taught this programme.

Ask also what they will show you at four weeks, and be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade. For MYP work the honest version of a four-week report is a before-and-after piece of the child's own work against the same criterion, not a grade prediction. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and does not publish success rates, because a figure built from the families who happened to stay tells you nothing about yours. An IB private tutor Andheri West families find through a school parents' group may be an excellent teacher of the subject who has never seen a criterion sheet, which is worth knowing before the first session rather than after the first report.

On the personal project specifically, ask where they draw the line, and listen for a clear boundary rather than enthusiasm. If a placement is not working, say so at the two-week or four-week review and we shortlist again at no cost. For MYP placements the commonest reason for a change is a tutor who teaches content well and never touches the criterion that was actually losing the marks.
bullets: MYP teaching experience evidenced, not inferred from international school work
Ask the candidate to name the four criteria in the subject group
Ask what a task-specific clarification is and what they do with it
A four-week report should be the child's own work before and after
The usual failure is good content teaching that ignores the weak criterion

sections.heading: The personal project in Year 5, and where a tutor's help stops
paragraphs: The personal project runs through Year 5 and is assessed on the process as much as on the outcome. A student sets a goal, plans how to reach it, produces something, and reports on what they did and what they learned, with a process journal running throughout. Schools assign a supervisor and the student meets them periodically. The commonest failure is not laziness. It is scope: a goal so ambitious that the product is unfinished, or so modest that there is nothing to report, and both are decided in the first few weeks.

That is where a tutor adds the most and where the boundary is clearest. A tutor can ask whether a goal is achievable in the time available, whether the student has a way of showing progress rather than just a finished object, and whether the journal is being kept in a form that will support the report. A tutor cannot choose the goal, make the product, write the report or manufacture journal entries after the fact. Schools check this work and the consequences land on the student. A tutor offering to help produce the deliverable is a risk, and the best ones say so before being asked.

The second place a tutor helps is the report, which students treat as a description and which is assessed as an account of a process. The report wants evidence of planning decisions, of problems encountered and of what was changed in response. A tutor can ask the questions that surface those sentences without writing any of them, which is coaching rather than ghostwriting, and the difference is visible to anybody reading carefully.

The timing in Mumbai is worth planning around. Personal project deadlines usually fall in the same stretch as unit assessments, so Year 5 families often want a short burst of extra sessions in one fortnight. Andheri West is the largest single source of tutoring enquiries in the Western Suburbs, and because Metro Line 1 and the Link Road let tutors cross from Ghatkopar or Malad without touching the highway, the pool here is deep enough to add that burst. Parents who search for the best IB tutor in Andheri West during Year 5 are usually looking for somebody who has supervised several projects, and a home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai families bring in for the project fortnight is a narrow and sensible use of a few hours. An IB tutor Mumbai households keep into the Diploma years often started there.
bullets: The project is assessed on process as much as on the product
Scope is decided in the first weeks and sets the ceiling
A tutor questions the goal, the evidence trail and the journal format
A tutor never chooses the goal, makes the product or writes the report
The report is an account of decisions, not a description of an object

sections.heading: MYP to DP: what to fix before Year 5 ends
paragraphs: Three things, and an IB MYP tutor in Andheri West will name the same three for almost every student in Mumbai. Algebraic fluency, because Diploma mathematics and the sciences assume it and the MYP can absorb a shaky base in a way the DP cannot. Timed writing, because criterion-marked coursework lets a student take their time and the DP will not. And independent long-range work, because the DP carries internal assessments and an Extended Essay that nobody will chase them through. A student who leaves Year 5 solid on those three has a far easier DP1 than one with better subject knowledge and none of them.

At four weeks into any MYP placement, the honest markers are these. The student can say which criterion they are weak on, in words rather than by letter. Homework happens without a negotiation each time. There is a written record of coverage and next steps. And there is one piece of their own work, marked against the weak criterion, that you can compare with a piece from week one. That comparison is the real evidence, and it usually shows change before a grade does.

At one term, expect movement on the weak criterion rather than across the board. A student who was losing marks on communication or on process documentation often improves quickly, because those are habits. A student with a genuine content gap in mathematics or in language analysis improves slowly and in the right direction. Treat a report of improvement on every criterion simultaneously as reassurance rather than reporting, and ask which criterion did not move.

Across the move into the DP, the limits are worth saying out loud. A tutor can build fluency, writing habits and self-management, and can make the subject choice conversation better informed. They cannot guarantee a smooth transition, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades. We will also say when the answer is fewer sessions: a Year 4 student with three subjects of tutoring, sport four evenings a week and a personal project ahead of them needs their week back more than they need another tutor.
bullets: Fix algebraic fluency, timed writing and long-range independence
Four weeks: the child names the criterion in words, not by letter
Compare one marked piece from week one with one from week four
Habit criteria move fast; content gaps move slowly and steadily
A child with four activities and three tutors needs their week back

sections.heading: Starting IB MYP home classes in Andheri West, Mumbai
paragraphs: Send five things: the MYP year, the subject group, the criterion named on the report, the real weekly timetable including sport and music, and which pocket of the area you live in. The timetable matters more here than on any other page, because MYP slots are early and short and the commonest cause of a failed placement is a slot that was never genuinely free.

Four items should be ready before the home tutor arrives, since Mumbai households routinely lose half of session one hunting for them. The most recent report with the criterion breakdown rather than just the grade. The current unit's task sheet with its task-specific clarifications. One or two marked pieces of the child's own work, chosen because they scored badly on the criterion in question. And, for a Year 5 student, whatever exists of the personal project journal so far.

The first session should be diagnostic and quite short on content. Expect the tutor to read the task sheet, read a marked piece with the child, and ask them to explain why a band was awarded rather than explaining it to them. Then one piece of work attempted against the weak criterion while the tutor watches. By the end they should name the criterion to be attacked and what a stronger response looks like for the next task. That is more useful than a term plan built on topics.

Practical items: a table in a shared room rather than a bedroom, the television off, and a sibling who is not watching something. Sort the visitor entry in week one if your building needs one for a standing weekly slot. Payment is per agreed block, there is no joining fee and no lock-in, and reshortlisting costs nothing. IB tutors near me Andheri West is the search most parents arrive on, and for the MYP the nearest competent candidate genuinely is the right answer, because short early sessions do not survive a long commute.

faqs.question: His grade looks fine but the report says a low band on criterion C. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: It means three of the four criteria were met well and one was not, and the combined grade hides that. Each MYP subject group is assessed against four criteria judged separately against published descriptors, so a student strong on knowledge and weak on communication receives a grade that looks like general mediocrity and is nothing of the kind. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown across the last two or three units. If the same criterion is low every time, that is your diagnosis, and it is usually a habit rather than a content gap.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups most often need a tutor?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, the Sciences and Language and Literature account for most enquiries, and the reasons differ. Mathematics because algebraic fluency gaps start limiting everything from Year 3. Sciences because investigation design and the processing and evaluating criterion are genuinely new skills that nobody is explicitly taught. Language and Literature because the step from summary to analysis is a real jump and students keep retelling the text. Design and the Arts generate fewer enquiries and a predictable one when they do: strong outcomes, weak documentation of the process, which is a criterion problem rather than a talent problem.

faqs.question: How do IB tuition fees in Andheri West work for an MYP student?
faqs.answer: MYP sessions are usually shorter and more frequent than Diploma sessions, so the per-session rate is typically lower and the weekly total may not be. Rates depend on the year group, the subject group, session length, travel distance and whether the session is in person or online. Because MYP slots are early and short, travel weighs more heavily on a tutor's willingness than it does for a Diploma student, which is another reason proximity matters. Ask each candidate to state rate, session length and travel assumption in one message so you compare the same thing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Oshiwara for a 5pm MYP session?
faqs.answer: Oshiwara is the best address in the area for this, because it sits on the Link Road and a tutor coming down from Goregaon or Malad arrives before the worst of the evening load. A 5pm start is also ideal for this age group, late enough for a break after school and early enough that concentration holds. Agree a ten-minute arrival window rather than a fixed time, and settle in advance that a heavy monsoon evening becomes a shorter online session instead of a cancellation, which matters more for a short session than a long one.

faqs.question: Is MYP 3 too early for a tutor?
faqs.answer: It is close to the ideal time, and more families should act then. Years 3 and 4 are where real subject demand arrives, and because there is no examination on the horizon nobody feels urgency, so gaps that would be easy to close get left for two years. Algebraic fluency in particular is built by volume over months, so a gap found in Year 3 can be closed quietly before it starts limiting the sciences and mathematics above it. The same gap found in the first Diploma year has to be fixed while the student is meeting much harder material.

faqs.question: How much help can a tutor give with the personal project?
faqs.answer: A great deal on scope, evidence and the report, and none at all on the product. A tutor can question whether the goal is achievable in the time available, whether the student has a way of showing progress rather than only a finished object, whether the process journal is being kept usefully, and whether the report accounts for the decisions made rather than describing the outcome. A tutor cannot choose the goal, make the product, write the report or manufacture journal entries. Schools check this work and the consequences land on the student, so a tutor offering more than this is a risk.

faqs.question: Will my child sit external examinations at the end of Year 5?
faqs.answer: That depends on your school, and you should ask the coordinator rather than assume. Some schools enter students for external MYP assessment at the end of Year 5 and others complete the programme through school-based assessment only. The answer changes how Year 5 should be planned, because an external component adds a timed-assessment dimension that school-based criterion work does not have. Ask the question in writing early in the year, and tell any tutor the answer, because a tutor planning for the wrong route will spend a term building the wrong habits.

faqs.question: She writes well but keeps losing marks. Where are they going?
faqs.answer: Usually to the criterion about organising or about producing text rather than the one about analysing. A student who writes fluently often writes a good essay that does not do what the criterion asked, most commonly retelling or summarising where analysis was required, or producing an unstructured piece where organisation is separately assessed. The fix is to work from the task-specific clarification for each task rather than from a general sense of good writing. Four weeks of planning answers against the clarification before writing them usually changes the band on that criterion.

faqs.question: Should we start preparing for the Diploma Programme during Year 5?
faqs.answer: Yes, and on three specific things rather than on content. Algebraic fluency, because Diploma mathematics and the sciences assume speed and accuracy the MYP can absorb without. Timed writing, because criterion-marked coursework allows a student to take their time and the Diploma will not. And independent long-range work, because the Diploma carries internal assessments and an Extended Essay that nobody chases a student through. A student who leaves Year 5 solid on those has an easier first Diploma year than one with better subject knowledge and none of them.

faqs.question: Can home classes work in the evening if he has sport after school?
faqs.answer: They can, but write down the real week before you commit to a slot, because this is the commonest reason an MYP placement collapses in week three. Children this age often have two or three activity afternoons, so the genuinely free windows are narrower than a parent's first answer suggests. A short session on a non-sport afternoon beats a longer one squeezed in after training, when a tired twelve-year-old gets little from it. Weekend mornings also work well for this age group and are easier to staff than late weekday slots.

faqs.question: My daughter is at JBCN International School, Oshiwara. Does the tutor need the task sheet?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single most useful thing you can send. MYP tasks come with task-specific clarifications that define what each criterion means for that particular piece of work, and a tutor working without them is guessing at the standard. Photograph the sheet and send it before the first session. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with JBCN International School, Oshiwara or any other school named here, so everything a tutor knows about your child's current unit comes from what you and your daughter provide.

faqs.question: What does Service as Action mean and does it need help?
faqs.answer: It is the expectation that students take action in their community as part of the programme, recorded and reflected on rather than graded like a subject. It rarely needs tutoring and occasionally needs organising, because students leave the reflection until the end and then cannot remember what they did or why it mattered. If a tutor helps at all, the useful contribution is building the habit of a short written reflection at the time rather than a reconstructed one later. Beyond that, this is a school-led part of the programme and a tutor should stay out of it.
